store_data.about_the_game:
Blobby Coins - The Board Game that mixes classic tabletop elements with simple strategy and luck. It's cute too

Play against up to 6 Blobbies and earn the most Coins. Collect move points on each tile and watch the moves of your opponents carefully. Plan every move or rush through successfully with some luck. Sometimes you find a treasure and sometimes you get stuck in a bear trap. Push your luck by playing on slot-machines and attacking other Blobbies to win their place. 

It doesn't matter which Blobby crosses the finish line first, but who made the most Coins. Just don't be the last Blobby on the board...

Thrilling gameplay

Each play is different as the resources on the tiles are generated randomly. The Blobbies dice their position in the beginning of the game. But the game can turn around instantly!

Just when you think you’ve already won, another Blobby finds a diamond. Every decision you make can determine whether you succeed or fail. But sometimes it’s just luck that decides.

Create your game

Choose between 3 or up to 6 players. Give them names, a color and dress them. Play against the computer only or mixed with local players. Play on the classic or metal game board. Make the game colorful, crazy and funny!

Earn rewards, shop and dress the Blobbies

Earn DCoins by playing against the computer with 3 different difficulty levels. The more players and the higher the difficulty, the more DCoins you win.

Go to the shop and spend the DCoins on dresses and accessories.

Vibrant graphics and adorable Blobbies

Get your daily sugar rush with the colorful design and funny cute Blobbies.

               

Couch multiplayer and gamepad support

Play with family and friends on the couch with one controller.

Leaderboard

The Hall of Fame remembers the Blobbies with the most earned Coins in history.

Linda Lastname is the leader of The Linda Society, a utopian coalition of vampires, monsters, aliens, and humans who have dedicated themselves to helping people. But that dedication is put to the test when a call for help from Beatrice and The Money Men sets Linda Lastname, Sandy Loam, Terror Mary, Cousin Jack, and Pio on a quest to destroy a vile group of anti-vampires known as The Pressure Men.

FEATURING

  • A High-Pressure Mystery: Discover the sickening truth behind The Pressure Men and their dark deeds.

  • Open-World Exploration: Visit over 160 locations across Canada. Towns, cities, and landmarks in all 13 provinces and territories, full of characters to talk to and interact with. 

  • Ultra-Reactive Dialogue: Engage in realistic, reactive conversation with characters that know who you are, where you’ve been, and what you’ve done.

  • Psycho Action: Take down The Pressure Men in a series of thrilling raids, shootouts, and action sequences.

  • Vampire Powers: Embrace the strength, speed, and shrinking ability commonly associated with vampires.

  • Side Quests: Take on odd jobs for your fellow citizens. No task is too small for The Linda Society!

  • Activities: Earn money in activities like fishing, skiing, target practice, casino games, and more.

store_data.about_the_game:
Survive the Deep Freeze. Reclaim Station 07.

Perched above a glacial fissure, Station 07 was once a pinnacle of deep-core research. Then the storm came. Routes vanished. You were abandoned by the surface. Now, you are the last soul at the core, separated from the ruins by a violent meltwater river.

The cold is not your only enemy. Hostile scavengers, resource depletion, and the horrific secrets of human experimentation lurk in the snow. Will you hold your ground, or push into the frozen unknown?

Key Features:
Our game actually supports both first-person and third-person views — you can switch anytime! (And yes… please ignore my terrible aim in first-person lol, I tried my best)

  • Base Building & Management: Restore the derelict Station 07. Manage critical power grids, heating systems, and oxygen to keep the base operational against the encroaching frost.

  • Deep Survival Mechanics: Every calorie and watt counts. Scavenge for scrap, hunt for food, or utilize advanced hydroponics to grow crops in a world where the sun never shines.

  • Dynamic Weather & Freezing Cycles: Adapt to a shifting environment. Prepare for the "Deep Freeze" periods where outdoor exploration becomes impossible, forcing you to rely on your base's stockpiles and integrity.

  • Tactical Choice & Combat: Face hostile human factions and "Cold-Adapted" biological monstrosities. Choose your path: stealthily "borrow" supplies from enemy camps, launch full-scale assaults, or negotiate fragile alliances with other major outposts.

  • Moral Dilemmas: Uncover the dark truth behind the station’s research. Encounter victims of human experimentation and decide: will you risk your own survival to shut down these atrocities, or turn a blind eye to stay alive?

  • Crafting & Modification: Use your technical expertise to turn industrial scrap into advanced weaponry and survival gear. Modify your equipment to withstand lower temperatures and deadlier foes.

  • Vast Exploration & Vehicle Mastery: Beyond the walls lies a massive, unforgiving arctic landscape. Deploy specialized vehicles to traverse the tundra, pilot aircraft for aerial reconnaissance, and master water-skimming craft across violent meltwater rivers.



    How will you lead? When the world turns to ice, humanity is the first thing to shatter.


    [Developer's Note]: Our vision for Station 07 is still expanding.

    Wishlist now — it definitely won’t disappoint you.

store_data.about_the_game:
● Overview

A revamped version of "TAILS GEAR", originally released in 2007, featuring high-resolution support, new systems, and rearranged background music.

A full-fledged 2.5D vertical-scrolling shooter characterized by the Tail Pod, an optional weapon that combines offense and defense.

While classified as a bullet hell type game, the Tail Pod's defensive shield allows for flexible gameplay.

● Story

Five years have passed since the war between the United Nations Forces and the giant corporation Astral Tech.

Hermann Arnold, a man who survived the war as an Astral Tech corporate pilot after undergoing nerve-steeling surgery, losing most of his pain sensations and emotions, lives on the run after the war's end, hearing the tormented cries of his fallen comrades in nightmares.

None of his comrades who were shot down and taken prisoner, or who surrendered at the end of the war, ever returned. Rumors spread that pilots enhanced with unknown technology were treated as spoils of war and not given the treatment of human beings.

While a world government, established from the International Unification Treaty Organization, promoted post-war reconstruction under the banners of a "government without borders" and "a leap into space," a horrifying truth was concealed behind the scenes. Ostensibly built as a symbol of the new unified government's power, these unmanned mobile weapons were actually devices that incorporated the soldiers as biological central units.

Reunited with Dr. Hegel, a technician who had also been in hiding to escape government pursuit, Arnold learns the full story. Realizing that his comrades' voices were not merely a nightmare, he resolves to fight to "liberate" them. Entrusted with the machine "DYNOSTAIL" by Dr. Hegel, its special weapon, the "Tail Pod," connects directly to Arnold's augmented nervous system, functioning like a second body.

Connecting his nerves to this machine, beyond the capabilities of an ordinary human, he takes flight into space, shrouded in a false peace, to kill his former comrades.

●Specifications

- The game is a 2.5D vertical-scrolling STG with 3D models.

- Deploy a shield with the tail pod and power up by absorbing enemy bullets.

- In addition to the arcade mode where you play all 5 stages in one go, a stage selection mode is also implemented, with 4 difficulty levels to choose from.

- You can choose between an HD arranged version of the background music and the classic version from 2007.

- Supports keyboard and gamepad controls.

store_data.about_the_game:
Heroes' Heaven is a party-based bullet heaven with a retro JRPG soul.

You don't control one hero. You control three.

Build a party from 8 unlockable classes — Fighter, Mage, Cleric, Swordsman, and four advanced tiers earned through battle. Your heroes auto-attack; you choose where to run, when to dodge, and which upgrades to take as your party levels up mid-run. Get the right weapons in the right hands and watch the screen erupt.

Five chapters. Five bosses. One shared HP bar.

From the Whispering Forest to the Void Throne, every chapter escalates the monster density and the stakes. Your party shares a single health pool — one wrong move punishes everyone equally, and the right composition can carry all three through situations none of them could survive alone.

Build. Upgrade. Evolve.

Combine weapons with passive relics to trigger evolutions mid-run — a throwing axe fused with a magnet becomes a permanent orbital storm. Fifteen base weapons, seven evolutions, and a class system that restricts and rewards your choices in equal measure.

The run ends. The progress doesn't.

Coins and skill points survive death. Hire new heroes from the Pub, level their skills at the Roster, and shop for equipment between runs. Every defeat leaves you a little stronger for the next attempt.

Push further when you're ready.

Clear all five chapters to unlock Hard Mode — fewer upgrade picks, tougher monsters, better rewards. Clear Hard to unlock Infinity Mode: an endless boss rush with escalating waves and a score to chase.

  • Party of 3 heroes with shared HP

  • team synergy matters

  • 8 classes including 4 advanced tiers with unique unlock conditions

  • 15 weapons + 7 evolution recipes unlocked mid-run

  • 5 chapters across distinct biomes, each with a hand-crafted boss

  • Persistent meta-progression: coin upgrades, equipment, hero leveling

  • Hard Mode + Infinity Mode endgame for score chasers

store_data.about_the_game:
Explore a detailed map featuring numerous locations and a dynamic day-night cycle. Every corner is filled with interactive elements that pull you deeper into the unique provincial atmosphere.

Along the way, you will meet three girls, each with her own distinct personality, struggles, and hobbies. To succeed, you must find a unique approach to each of them and navigate their individual questlines.

Beyond romantic interests, you can build meaningful connections with friends, relatives, and a diverse cast of characters, each featuring their own unique personality and dedicated questline. The game is packed with interactive depth: from shopping for various items and engaging in micromanagement gameplay to branching dialogues where your choices truly shape the unfolding narrative.

This isn’t an attempt to reconstruct reality, but rather to capture a specific mood. It’s an echo of an era when cities were less polished, yet somehow felt more alive. Today, the streets are cleaner, the facades brighter, and the spaces more convenient. And yet, the memory holds onto the warmth of those courtyards, stairwells, and vacant lots where an entire generation grew up.

Always Summer Out Here is a journey into that very feeling. It’s a place that never truly existed, but one that everyone will recognize.

store_data.about_the_game:
In Nodebreak, you control an orb of energy —a high velocity surge contained within a lethal circuit. Your existence is defined by the circuit, and your survival depends on your ability to navigate its complex web of interconnected branching nodes at breakneck speeds.

PLOT YOUR COURSE. WAIT FOR THE OPENING. LAUNCH.

Here, survival is measured in millisecond precision after launches at breakneck speeds in-between nodes. Every move you make is an explosive dash through a high-velocity web, where route planning meets lightning fast reactions and execution. As you navigate this complex gauntlet of nodes, you must read the environment in real-time, choose your perfect route, while making split second decisions, and use all the powers at your disposal to turn the tides in your favor. Spatial awareness is your best friend, and perfect timing is what keeps you alive.

LAUNCH. DIE. REPEAT. SUCCEED.

The world is easy to understand. Hard to time. Difficult to master. The challenge lies in reading the map, making smart routing decisions at branching intersections, perfectly timing your launches, and having split second reactions to survive a brutal gauntlet of environmental hazards. Yes, you will die. That just makes reaching the end that much sweeter.

YOU ARE NOT HELPLESS.

The world may be against you, everything might be trying to kill you, but you have your own suite of powers. You have a limited stamina pool for each of your powers, but using them smartly is the only way you survive.

MOMENTUM ARREST

While you rocket between nodes automatically, you aren't defenseless mid-flight. By using the MOMENTUM ARREST, you can physically contain your momentum and pause on the circuit to let a hazard sweep past with millimeters to spare. But be careful, a strict stamina pool prevents overuse. Once your stamina depletes, your momentum immediately resumes, throwing you forward regardless of the danger ahead.

PLANNED POWERS

Although these are not there in the game yet, we have plans to include these powers to provide more options for your gameplay.

  • TIME DILATION

  • BLINK

  • SHIELDS

SLEEK AND UNFORGIVING.

Nodebreak features a minimalist, highly readable geometric aesthetic where the game state is always visually clear. The path forward glows bright teal, the hazards have an ominous red glow. Your blue ball of energy awaits your command. The world may be hard, but it is fair.

store_data.about_the_game:
In Be The Rocket Bucket you pilot one of the most advanced pieces of Llama technology in the world. The Rocket Bucket is nigh-invincible super powered rocket propelled vessel of destruction. Made of a tungsten carbon fiber structure for strength and light weight. When this bucket goes fast enough it can smash through just about any wall, fence, building, or enemy. Nothing like the rocket bucket has ever been seen before. Bullets will be laughed at as they bounce off the hard surface of the super strong bucket. Should the rocket bucket's tank explode your protective suit should save you. The Llama's of Peace take no responsibility for damage or harm that might happen while operating the rocket bucket.

Massive maps, huge bases to destroy, diverse sets of enemies, tons of upgrades for the bucket, and a battleship to upgrade. 

Unlock many levels in a variety of landscapes and weather conditions. Desert, forest, tropical, and mountains with snow, rain, lighting, and wind are but a few of the diverse levels included.

This game can be a shooter, strategy, speed running, bullet hell, easy going, simulator depending on how the player decides to play. To keep the player on their feet some light elements of strategy were carefully though through. It is easy going, because if you don't really care about your score, you could take your time in each level enjoying the beautiful trees and beaches. This is open as possible to let the player play as they want. Side missions are available to get more money, but again side missions will cost more of the players time. No side missions will mean less money to get better upgrades. This way difficulty scales with the speed the player decides to play. Speed runners will have the hardest time.

Realistic physics are programmed throughout the game at every level. The buckets gravitational pull to the planet realistically changes based on it's orbital velocity and altitude. The air resistance changes based on the cross sectional area of the bucket, velocity, and air density. As you go higher the air density changes realistically effecting air resistance. Bullets give kick back. Mass of the bucket effects maneuverability. Changes in the buckets guns, fuel tank, and wheel will change the buckets mass accordingly. As fuel is used mass will also change. This is not some quickly made asset flip. This is a work of love over 10 years in the making.

Additional Note: I am a self appointed inventor. The idea of the rocket bucket is originally based on something that could actually be made in real life. The rockets are at a level where they would push through the center of gravity of the bucket. The one problem would be the time it could stay in the air would probably not be nearly as long as what is shown in the game. Some rules have to be bent for a fun game. Hope you all enjoy it.

store_data.about_the_game:
Become a Magic Wand and Begin a Legendary Journey

“Find your master.”

A mysterious voice awakens you from a long slumber. The world has fallen into chaos and despair, and people await a hero.

You become a self-moving magic wand and embark on a dangerous journey to find your master. Reach the top of each stage while avoiding endless platforms, deadly traps, and enemies determined to knock you down.

As your journey continues, the stages become even harsher, testing your concentration and control.

Climb the Platforms

Spin and jump your magic wand to climb upward. Precise timing and delicate control are essential for survival.

A single mistake could send you falling all the way down.

Defeat the Bosses

Powerful bosses await at the end of every stage. Defeat them to open the portal leading to the next stage.

Bosses will use relentless attacks and patterns to knock you down endlessly.

Use Your Skills

As you progress through your journey, you will acquire a variety of skills. Using the right skill at the right moment is crucial for overcoming dangerous areas and defeating bosses.

Use your skills to forge your own path to victory.

store_data.about_the_game:
Jianghu Cangfeng is a martial arts turn-based party-building roguelike RPG set in a dangerous jianghu world.

Lead your heroes into mysterious realms filled with battles, random events, treasure, rest points, and difficult choices. Every step consumes supplies, and every encounter tests your planning, martial arts setup, equipment choices, and resource management.

The game features techniques from multiple martial arts sects, as well as wandering jianghu styles. Skills differ in damage types, cooldowns, energy costs, buffs, debuffs, dispels, cleanses, interruptions, and channeling effects. Build each character around their role, combine techniques with equipment, and adapt your strategy to different enemies.

During each expedition, you may gain temporary raid perks, equipment rewards, and event outcomes that change your run. Choosing when to take risks, when to conserve supplies, and how to prepare for key battles is central to survival.

This is not a game about simply overpowering enemies with numbers. It is about making choices under pressure, shaping your martial arts build, and slowly forging a party that can survive the hidden dangers of the jianghu.

Key Features:

- Martial arts turn-based combat

- Party building with multiple playable characters

- Techniques from different sects and wandering jianghu styles

- Character growth shaped by skills, equipment, and temporary raid perks

- Expedition-based exploration with supply management

- Random events, treasure, rest points, and combat encounters

- Combat mechanics including buffs, debuffs, dispels, cleanses, interruptions, and channeling

- Strategic choices that shape each run

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to your new job at Bowl City High School! You could have sworn the place has been abandoned your whole life, but you need the paycheck. The teachers there do get a bit quirky at night, so you must be on guard. Don't worry though, Mr. Phone is there to give you instructions to survive the night, and with more than 8 teachers to keep track of, you must listen carefully: use the cameras to check the teacher's positions and plan ahead, complete your homework to stop Mr. Math, block off vents to keep the teachers at bay, and use hiding spots to sneakily avoid the teachers. The school runs on limited power, so limiting consumption is key, and Micheal Science doesn't appreciate your power usage, so make sure to keep your usage down to a minimum. Most importantly, however... you must stop Mr. Gut... 

Once you've made it through the first 6 nights, overtime is an option, but it is unadvised due to extreme safety hazards. Other nights are available as well, like the custom night for extra challenges and rewards.


Can you survive five nights at Bowl City High School?

This game was created using Godot game engine.

store_data.about_the_game:
Bloomtide

Every morning, a 9×9 board reshuffles from your filling pool. Apples, lightning, hawks, cherry blossoms — what ends up next to what decides how much you earn today. You have one job: pay the rent.

But the real game is turning "enough" into an explosion.

Core Loop

  • The board reshuffles every day — same pool, new layout. Adjacent relationships create new synergies each run.

  • Event queue resolution — growth, devour, movement, decay, burst. One event triggers the next, chaining into exponential payoffs.

  • Daily 3-pick (CoreItem) — add a new symbol type, or weight an existing one. Slowly bend the random board toward your archetype.

  • Rent at the end of each cycle — survive the rent check, then pick a BuffItem or EffectItem to amplify whatever build is forming. Cycles get longer as you progress; rent keeps climbing.

Three Strategy Layers

  • Board (CoreItem) — define what can show up on your board.

  • Environment (EffectItem) — Snowy Mountain accelerates growth. Deep Sea strengthens devouring. Match your archetype.

  • Equipment (BuffItem) — multiplier wands, xmult rings. Take a working build and break the numbers.

"I went growth-fruits → I need the snowy mountain → I need the multiplier wand." When the build clicks, you feel the machine working for you.

Two Modes

  • Campaign — 12 rent payments to win. A guided ramp through every mechanic.

  • Endless — rent stops scaling at run 14. All items unlocked. No survival pressure — just "how far can my build push the numbers?"

Why You Won't Stop

  • Numbers go up — hard. A modifier pipeline (chips_add → chips_mul → mult_add → mult_mul → xmult) takes a good hand from dozens to millions in a single resolve.

  • Hidden combos to discover. A hawk eating a snake poisons the field. A cherry blossom hitting zero blows up everyone. Hundreds of cross-item interactions waiting.

  • Every run is different. Archetypes × environments × equipment = a vast space of viable builds.

  • Simple rules, emergent depth. Each item is readable at a glance. The combinations are not.

  • Stylized symbol art. Every piece is readable at a glance — high information density, zero recognition cost.

store_data.about_the_game:
A signal under the ice. A crew with too little time. A choice Earth will not understand.


Kryonull is a cinematic science-fiction visual novel set on Europa, the frozen moon of Jupiter. The expedition ship Sirena descends toward a thermal anomaly beneath the ice and a repeating radio pattern that sounds less like noise with every minute.

Every decision changes the mission profile: preserve the relay or chase the signal, drill slowly or force a narrow window, answer the ocean or leave in silence. Trust, hull integrity, oxygen, evidence, and biological risk shape the route to one of several endings.

Features

  • Branching sci-fi story inspired by tense first-contact cinema.
  • Multiple routes and endings based on mission discipline, crew trust, evidence, and risk.
  • Russian and English text support.
  • Voice acting for both Russian and English versions.
  • Original 1920x1080 background art for Europa, the under-ice ocean, laboratories, orbit, and mission-critical scenes.

For players who like

Quiet space horror, philosophical science fiction, hard choices, crew drama, alien contact, and endings that remember what you risked.

store_data.about_the_game:
Cultist is a turn-based card game with an anthropological theme that captures the religions and history of the ancient Mediterranean and Middle Eastern world. Through the game, players can become powerful religions and ideas that endure the trials of time, or become mere traces left in relics.

About Cultist

The cards in the game each represent diverse doctrines and ideas befitting their historical background. They grow and develop based on the participation of new cultists. What begins as a simple Beliefs, or merely a collection of those, expands through play into cults and sects, eventually branching into forms resembling actual classical religions.

The overall flow of the game varies each time according to the cards used and their sequence, but the common theme lies in the interactions, commonalities, and mutual influences among early religions.

Religion and It's cultists

Cultists are the source that provides you with the doctrines that strengthen you, but they also serve as the substance that sustains you as an idea itself. When a Cultist is flipped over and used as doctrine, it can no longer function as a Cultist; and after the first turn, any religion that loses all of its Cultists is defeated. Holding many Cultists is a way to protect yourself from other aggressive religions and ideas, and at the same time an excellent strategy for adding compelling ideas to your religious community.

There are various ways to add Cultists.

1. The basic method

By default, every turn each player has one opportunity to draw cards at the start of their turn. At this point, they choose one of the following:

  a. Draw Cards: Look at three cards from your deck and add one to your religion. Discard the remaining two.

  b. Trade: Take one card of your choice from among the discarded cards.

2. Additional methods

Some cards allow you to draw additional cards in various situations, such as every turn or when a card is flipped. When the text states "perform an additional Draw Cards," follow action a; when it states "perform an additional Trade," follow action b. Unlike the basic method described above, these additional methods do not have to be performed at the start of the turn; once their conditions are met, this opportunity may be used at any point before the turn ends. Be cautious, however—cards that allow you to gain additional cards can be dangerous.

Deck Building

The Early Access version of this game comes with four pre-built decks that will help you get a feel for play.

However, building your own deck will deepen your understanding of the cards and help to find unconventional strategies. A deck consists of 31 cards including 1 starting card, and you may include up to 3 copies of any given non-starting card. There are no other restrictions on card selection: you may use cards from a wide range of religious themes, or focus on a concentrated build. But be careful—if you don't check the required symbols, you may find that cards you've added to your deck can't actually be played. Always check the types and number of symbols a card provides, and consider whether they can meet the symbol requirements of your other cards.

A deck consists of 31 cards including 1 starting card, and you may include up to 3 copies of any given non-starting card. There are no other restrictions on card selection: you may use cards from a wide range of religious themes, or focus on a concentrated build. But be careful—if you don't check the required symbols, you may find that cards you've added to your deck can't actually be played. Always check the types and number of symbols a card provides, and consider whether they can meet the symbol requirements of your other cards.

Card Mechanics: Sacrifice and Destroy

Besides drawing additional cards, flipping cards produces various effects on the field, and you must consider these factors when building a deck.

Sacrifice

Some cards require Sacrifice. Sacrifice is performed on Cultist cards you own, and once triggered, the selected Cultist card is immediately destroyed. Cards and effects that can be used by sacrificing a Cultist card carry powerful effects capable of turning the tide of the game.

Destroy

Some cards have a direct impact on other players by destroying their Cultist cards. Because this is an extremely powerful mechanic, such cards may require additional conditions—for example, possessing greater Military Power than the opponent, or holding another combo card.

Don't worry. Cultist cards that have been sacrificed or destroyed are not removed from the game; they move into the trade pile, where they may be introduced to other players.

In addition, some cards carry various keywords, and these provide important information for play.

  • The [Split] keyword opens up space to form a new sect when the card is flipped. Through different sects, you can efficiently strengthen your religion and reduce the risks of certain cards. You can have up to 3 sects.

  • The [Feat] keyword is used on cards with very powerful effects, and only one such card may exist in a flipped state on a single player's field. Using these at the right moment is crucial.

  • The [Echo] keyword takes effect when an opponent declares destroy on this card while it is unflipped. In that case, instead of being destroyed, the card is flipped without cost and immediately provides a benefit to the player holding it. This is a powerful bluff, and punishes plays that destroy opponents' card.

  • The [Crisis] keyword triggers while the card is in the deck: if a card with this keyword appears during the Draw Cards phase, it must be selected.

  • The [Revelation] keyword triggers when deck have been exhausted; cards with this keyword can only be drawn one at a time, and once acquired, must be flipped immediately to use their effect.

  • Cards with the [Sacrifice] keyword require sacrificing another Cultist card in order to be flipped.

  • Ultimately, you must build a powerful deck that can win either by completing the Pantheon or by eliminating all of the other players' Cultist cards.

Symbols and the Pantheon

The cards have various symbols matching their contents and effects. Each symbol is one of the following: Influence, Unity, Polytheistic, Monotheistic, or Military Power. These respectively indicate how expansionistic a religion is, how politically unified it is, how strongly polytheistic or monotheistic it is, and how militarily strong it is.

To flip and activate most cards, you must possess enough of these symbols. The top portion of a card shows the types and number of symbols required, while the bottom shows the types and number of symbols you gain by holding the card flipped. These symbols do not disappear while the card is held flipped; they are considered continuously possessed.

Monotheistic

Monotheistic cards consist mainly of Abrahamic religions and the cards that influenced them. Compared to polytheistic cards, they have a more exclusive character; they grow stronger as the game progresses, but the symbols they require also increase steeply. Late-game cards generally have high Military Power and make it easy to win by destroying opponents' Cultists. However, gaining Pantheons is difficult. Early-game cards are designed to defend opponents' interference and enable steady growth.

Polytheistic

Polytheistic cards consist of different faiths from various cultural regions. They appear separately in the early stages, but as the game progresses they fuse together and develop composite divinities. In the game, polytheistic cards have relatively low symbol requirements but come with various restrictive conditions. Resolving these restrictions may require using cards with different religious cultures together. The low symbol requirements buy time to score cards from other religious cultures. Victory is typically achieved by gaining Pantheons with the powerful combo play.

Unity

Unity indicates how well a religion can rally its members together. A religion with high Unity manages the dissatisfaction of its members and makes remarkable feats possible through individual sacrifice. In the game, Unity is allotted to cards representing exclusive religious cards whose growth is driven by strong cohesion. Most cards that require Unity have a high-risk, high-reward structure, and are designed to enable rapid, aggressive development based on a few key cards.

Influence

Influence indicates how expansionistic a religion is. An open religion that spreads explosively in a short period of time can be considered a religion of high Influence. In the game, Influence is concentrated on the cards of religions that have continuously changed by absorbing other cultures, rather than religions that grew through internal cohesion. Cards that require Influence do not produce powerful effects in a short time, but they stabilize the card supply and can demonstrate their effect when combined with other cards over the long term.

Military Power

Military Power indicates how much influence one can project over other religious communities. A player with strong Military Power can interfere more frequently with other players. They can destroy Cultist cards, restrict certain plays, and gain more advantages in turn order. Because Military Power cards are divided among cards of different religious cultures, achieving high Military Power may require various kinds of symbols. They are not distributed evenly and the timing at which they can be acquired also differs, so they must be considered first when designing a deck.

Pantheon

Some cards possess feats and influence that endure through the passage of time. These are represented by a temple-shaped Pantheon icon, and holding seven or more allows you to win after the end of a turn. Unlike other symbols, Pantheons are not required to activate cards, but they are necessary for victory, which can make them relatively difficult to acquire.

In the game there are diverse beliefs and the diverse religions that can be built from them. These religions are not sharply distinguished from one another and may follow different historical trajectories depending on the players' moment-to-moment choices that may be either constructive or self-destructive. The various ideas are contained within the cards.

Can you outgrow the world that contains yourself and become much bigger?

  • Cards with the [Sacrifice] keyword require sacrificing another Cultist card in order to be flipped.

  • Ultimately, you must build a powerful deck that can win either by completing the Pantheon or by eliminating all of the other players' Cultist cards.

Symbols and the Pantheon

The cards have various symbols matching their contents and effects. Each symbol is one of the following: Influence, Unity, Polytheistic, Monotheistic, or Military Power. These respectively indicate how expansionistic a religion is, how politically unified it is, how strongly polytheistic or monotheistic it is, and how militarily strong it is.

To flip and activate most cards, you must possess enough of these symbols. The top portion of a card shows the types and number of symbols required, while the bottom shows the types and number of symbols you gain by holding the card flipped. These symbols do not disappear while the card is held flipped; they are considered continuously possessed.

Monotheistic

Monotheistic cards consist mainly of Abrahamic religions and the cards that influenced them. Compared to polytheistic cards, they have a more exclusive character; they grow stronger as the game progresses, but the symbols they require also increase steeply. Late-game cards generally have high Military Power and make it easy to win by destroying opponents' Cultists. However, gaining Pantheons is difficult. Early-game cards are designed to defend opponents' interference and enable steady growth.

Polytheistic

Polytheistic cards consist of different faiths from various cultural regions. They appear separately in the early stages, but as the game progresses they fuse together and develop composite divinities. In the game, polytheistic cards have relatively low symbol requirements but come with various restrictive conditions. Resolving these restrictions may require using cards with different religious cultures together. The low symbol requirements buy time to score cards from other religious cultures. Victory is typically achieved by gaining Pantheons with the powerful combo play.

Unity

Unity indicates how well a religion can rally its members together. A religion with high Unity manages the dissatisfaction of its members and makes remarkable feats possible through individual sacrifice. In the game, Unity is allotted to cards representing exclusive religious cards whose growth is driven by strong cohesion. Most cards that require Unity have a high-risk, high-reward structure, and are designed to enable rapid, aggressive development based on a few key cards.

Influence

Influence indicates how expansionistic a religion is. An open religion that spreads explosively in a short period of time can be considered a religion of high Influence. In the game, Influence is concentrated on the cards of religions that have continuously changed by absorbing other cultures, rather than religions that grew through internal cohesion. Cards that require Influence do not produce powerful effects in a short time, but they stabilize the card supply and can demonstrate their effect when combined with other cards over the long term.

Military Power

Military Power indicates how much influence one can project over other religious communities. A player with strong Military Power can interfere more frequently with other players. They can destroy Cultist cards, restrict certain plays, and gain more advantages in turn order. Because Military Power cards are divided among cards of different religious cultures, achieving high Military Power may require various kinds of symbols. They are not distributed evenly and the timing at which they can be acquired also differs, so they must be considered first when designing a deck.

Pantheon

Some cards possess feats and influence that endure through the passage of time. These are represented by a temple-shaped Pantheon icon, and holding seven or more allows you to win after the end of a turn. Unlike other symbols, Pantheons are not required to activate cards, but they are necessary for victory, which can make them relatively difficult to acquire.

In the game there are diverse beliefs and the diverse religions that can be built from them. These religions are not sharply distinguished from one another and may follow different historical trajectories depending on the players' moment-to-moment choices that may be either constructive or self-destructive. The various ideas are contained within the cards.

Can you outgrow the world that contains yourself and become much bigger?
store_data.short_description: Cultist is card game about begining of the religions and the way they grow, interact and even become immortal. Can you outgrow the world that contains yourself and become much bigger?

Bet on every card flip in this cozy roguelike deckbuilder.

Will the next card be Higher, Lower, or Equal? Predict right and stack your score. Predict wrong and watch your run unravel. Hi-Lo Roguelike is a card-flipping, joker-stacking, story-telling adventure where every choice could be your last.

Climb a procedurally generated map of battles, shops, events, and treasures. Collect 32 unique jokers, build absurd score-multiplying combos, and find your perfect run. Then do it all over again, every run is different.

FEATURES

Master the Hi-Lo Mechanic, Predict if the next card is higher, lower, or equal. Simple to learn, impossible to master.

32 Unique Jokers to Collect, From the simple Diamond Hunter to the run, defining Phoenix, each joker rewires how you play.

15 Story-Driven Events, Encounter a lost puppy, a card-sharking monkey, a whispering crystal lizard. Every choice, Brave, Smart, or Coward, changes your run.

Roguelike Map Progression, Battle nodes, shops, treasures, elites, and a final boss. Choose your path wisely.

Skill Over Luck, Use Peek, Skip, and Insurance abilities to read the deck. The more you know, the better you bet.

Pastel Cozy Aesthetic, A handcrafted cartoon world full of charm, soft colors, and surprisingly tense decisions.

Endless Replayability, Procedurally generated maps, randomized jokers, branching events. No two runs alike.

If you love score-stacking deckbuilders, run-based roguelikes, and cozy story-driven card games, Hi-Lo Roguelike was built for you.

One deck. Endless decisions. Will you bet it all?

store_data.about_the_game:
A decade and almost 1 million mobile downloads later, Skillful Pixel Dungeon comes to Steam.

Dive into a challenging roguelike RPG where every run tells a different story. Choose from four distinct classes, each offering unique active and passive abilities that open up multiple playstyles. Whether you favor brute force, precision, or strategy, no two journeys feel the same.

Descend through 25 procedural generated levels filled with danger, secrets, and loot, culminating in five formidable bosses that will test your mastery. With ever-changing dungeons and meaningful build variety, Skillful Pixel Dungeon delivers a fresh, high-stakes experience every time you play.

Pick one of 4 classes

Warrior

The warrior relies on brute strength and toughness in combat. His skills are close combat oriented leveraging melee weapons and high durability. The gladiators excel in single melee combat while berserkes are all around strong and can attack multiple enemies in one attack.

Mage

The mage relies on magic and minions to battle the forces of evil. The battle mage subclass boosts wand damage and allows using mana to absorb damage while the warlock turns his minions into even more feared beasts.

Rogue

The rogue relies on stealth and speed. Some rogues are so fast they can create copies of themselves while others excel in stealth allowing them to instantly take out sleeping enemies.

Huntress

The huntress is the weakest of all physically but her ranged skills make sure no enemy comes to close. The huntress's knowledge with the bow gives her access to skills like fletching and kneeshot. The warden is capable of shooting two arrows in one go as well as hunting animals passively for food. Snipers are capable of putting enemies to sleep and even attaching explosives to arrows.

Mercenaries

The hero is not alone on his quest. He can hire one of five mercenaries to aid him on his quest. The mercs come with basic equipment that may need replacement as the levels get tougher.

Brute

The toughest of mercenaries. A brute is slow but capable of soaking a lot of damage. He is also of capable of carrying any item in the carry slot.

Wizard

The wizard is physically weak but can summon rats in combat.

Thief

The thief is very fast and relies on stealth. His attack may poison enemies.

Archer

The archer does not have a lot of health so she attacks from distance. She has a habit of attacking kneecaps.

Archer Maiden

The elite version of archer mercs. Archer maidens are more expensive but worth the investment.

store_data.about_the_game:
Idle Defense throws you into a hypnotic, minimalist arena where neon cubes of every color surge toward you. You can crush them yourself or build an automatic defense grid that grinds them down while you strategize.

This isn't just another idle game. It's a deep, neon-soaked loop of progression, prestige, and pure destruction.

KEY FEATURES:

  • Dual-Mode Destruction – Play actively by smashing cubes with your mouse, or go idle by purchasing automated turrets that fire non-stop. Both paths are viable. Both are rewarding.

  • 7 Cube Colors = 7 Currencies – Each color has its own resource, its own upgrade tree, and its own behavior. All seven can swarm your screen at once. Manage the chaos.

  • 25 Base Upgrades – Split across three core pillars:
    Cube upgrades, Idle turret upgrades, Mouse upgrades.

  • Prestige System – Reset your progress to permanently boost your base upgrade power with multipliers and raise upgrade base levels. Each prestige makes the next run noticeably stronger.

  • Tiers Difficulty – Complete specific objectives to ascend to higher Tiers. Each new Tier ramps up the danger—and the rewards.

  • Perk System – Unlock passive skills and unique bonuses based on your total enemies defeated. The more you kill, the more specialized your build becomes.

  • Boss Waves – Summon massive, high-risk waves at will. Defeat the boss to claim exclusive rewards that normal cubes never drop.

  • Minimalist. Neon. Satisfying. – No clutter. No distraction. Just a grid, vivid cubes, sharp particle effects, and clean UI. It looks simple. It plays deep.

Add Idle Defense to your wishlist and dive into the neon grind very soon!

store_data.about_the_game:
About Hearts in Open Water


Hearts in Open Water is an adult romance visual novel set aboard M/Y Halcyon, a 55-meter superyacht working a high-pressure Mediterranean charter season while quietly preparing for a looming sale. You play as Reeve, a disciplined ex-Royal Navy captain whose authority is absolute on the water—and whose job depends on a single line in a closing memo.

Over twelve weeks of procedures, port calls, and midnight requests that never make it into the official log, three women step across thresholds only the captain controls. Choose one route, live one romance—and learn what a season-ending decision really costs.

Meet the Cast




Cosima — The Owner's Suite
Cosima Lasry is the perfectly photographed wife of a hedge-fund titan—and the most strategic person on the yacht. As her marriage approaches a contractual deadline, she begins using the vessel's routines to carve out an escape that no one is allowed to notice. To Reeve, she is both principal and pressure point: a woman who understands his discretion, and knows exactly how to ask for it.



Anouk — The Survey
A senior yacht sales broker with a six-figure commission on the line, Anouk boards Halcyon as the buyer's observer—clipboard in hand, reputation sharpened to a blade. Her closing memo contains a retention line that can keep Reeve in command or quietly end his tenure. Their relationship is a controlled collision of ambition and attraction: two people trained to keep everything on record, tempted by what happens when the record is closed.



Tully — The Interior
Promoted to Chief Stewardess on Reeve's signature, Tully runs the yacht's luxury like a mission—fast, flawless, and almost invisible until she chooses not to be. Behind the polished service is a private urgency: her sister's chemo back in Brisbane, paid for by the very season she cannot afford to leave. With Reeve, her romance is built on mutual competence and late-night honesty—two professionals choosing each other in the only gaps the job allows.

Key Features


  • Single-choice romance routes with high-stakes intimacy: commit to one love interest and follow a focused, escalating relationship shaped by your decision.
  • A superyacht romance grounded in power, protocol, and consequence: maritime law, chain of command, and professional distance are the central tension.
  • The Logbook as a living threat: what gets recorded, what gets omitted, and what can never be erased drives the story's suspense.
  • Three distinct romantic arcs, three distinct worlds: The Interior, The Survey, and The Owner's Suite.
  • A seasonal clock you cannot stop: the sale closes, the charter ends, and the vessel moves on—no matter what you choose.
  • Each romance route includes explicit adult scenes.

store_data.about_the_game:
Galaxiwilds is a narrative-driven space exploration experience focused on discovery, first contact, and uncovering the unknown.

Reality is breaking.

Across multiple universes, rifts tear through space, black holes behave unpredictably, and entire systems collapse without warning. These phenomena are not random—they are connected.

Your mission is not to conquer.
It is to understand.

Travel between universes, chart strange systems, and make contact with 75 unique alien civilizations, each with their own culture, history, technology, and perspective on the unfolding crisis.

Some will share knowledge.
Some will grant you new abilities.
Some will offer allies you can call upon—individuals with their own personalities, insights, and stories to tell.

As your network grows, so does your understanding of what lies beyond the rifts… and what may be causing them.

But this is not a guided journey.

Clues are not handed to you. Coordinates are not saved. Information must be observed, remembered, and recorded.

The truth is out there—but only if you’re paying attention.

store_data.about_the_game:
Medieval vs Machines is an incremental tower defense auto-battler about building a medieval army to defend your castle against a massive invasion of machines from another dimension.

Your kingdom was peaceful… until the sky split open and strange mechanical armies came pouring through. Robots, cyber soldiers, tanks, and war machines now march toward your land. Your only choice is to raise an army, strengthen your defenses, and fight back.

Build your forces from humble medieval troops into a powerful fantasy army. Recruit warriors, lancers, archers, knights, and even mighty monsters to protect your castle. Every unit has a role in battle, and every upgrade brings you closer to surviving the next wave.

Build Your Medieval Army

Start small, then grow into a full battlefield force. Add more troops, improve their stats, and unlock new ways to fight the machine horde.

Train and upgrade:

  • Sword-wielding warriors

  • Long-range archers

  • Charging lancers

  • Heavy armored knights

  • Powerful fantasy monsters

  • Defensive towers and castle upgrades

As your army grows, battles become larger, louder, and more chaotic.

Defend Against the Machine Horde

The machines do not stop. Each wave brings more enemies, stronger units, and deadlier attacks. Fight against robotic soldiers, futuristic weapons, armored vehicles, and cybernetic monsters from another dimension.

Your medieval army may look simple, but with the right upgrades, even swords and bows can stand against steel and lasers.

Incremental Progression

Medieval vs Machines is built around satisfying incremental growth. Earn resources from battle, spend them on upgrades, and come back stronger every wave.

Upgrade your troops, improve your castle, unlock new units, and push deeper into the machine invasion. Every run makes your army stronger and your defenses harder to break.

Unlock Skill Trees

Customize your strategy through skill trees. Improve your troops, boost your towers, unlock special upgrades, and shape your army around your favorite playstyle.

Focus on overwhelming numbers, powerful elite units, stronger defenses, faster attacks, or monster-based chaos.

Massive Auto-Battler Battles

Once the battle begins, your army fights automatically. Watch huge pixel-art battles unfold as medieval soldiers clash against futuristic machines.

Battles can grow into massive 100 vs 100+ fights filled with arrows, blades, bullets, explosions, monsters, and robots.

Your job is to prepare the army.
Their job is to hold the line.

Charming Pixel Art Style

Enjoy a fun contrast between cute medieval fantasy units and colorful cyberpunk machines. The battlefield is full of personality, from tiny knights and archers to giant monsters and mechanical invaders.

Key Features

  • Incremental tower defense gameplay

  • Auto-battler style combat

  • Build and upgrade a medieval army

  • Defend your castle against machine hordes

  • Recruit warriors, lancers, archers, knights, and monsters

  • Unlock skill trees and customize your troops

  • Large-scale 100 vs 100+ pixel-art battles

  • Medieval fantasy vs cyberpunk machine theme

  • Charming pixel art and chaotic battlefield action

Defend the Castle

The machines want your land.
Your army stands in their way.

Build your kingdom. Upgrade your troops. Hold the castle.

This is your land. Defend it.

store_data.about_the_game:
⚠️ NO-HORROR MODE AVAILABLE

This game includes an optional mode where jump scares and psychological elements can be disabled, allowing you to play using only the card‑game mechanics.

In the Exiled Prison, scares remain active, as they are part of the core challenge.

Memo R.I.P. is a first‑person psychological horror card game for 1–4 players with real‑time voice. Every match blends strategy, tension, and dynamic scares. The game features 6 rooms, each containing 150 unique scares, for a total of 900 events that react to your Madness Bar. The higher it gets, the more vulnerable you become: you’ll see the entity that lives in the room, hear it, feel it, and fall for its distractions—forgetting your hand’s value and losing the match.

First‑person card gameplay

You play on cozy‑futuristic tables inside a spaceship, lit by stable or unstable neon depending on the room’s state. Each room has its own entity, its own behavior, and its own way of watching and manipulating you. You don’t know which one you’ll get. You don’t know which card will wake it up. You don’t know when it will move behind you.

Dynamic psychological horror

The Blackbell System alters the rules in real time. AI fills empty player slots. Vivox transmits your breathing, doubts, and reactions… but during Blackbell, you won’t hear your teammates—yet they will hear you. The six card‑game variants completely change the pace of each match.

The Exiled Prison

Winning a match is not the end. At certain levels, the trial of the Exiled Boss awaits: you wake up in the Exiled Prison, an explorable map inspired by PT, Visage, and Resident Evil. Find the Four Cards of Madness, solve puzzles, and survive the whispers trying to break your mind. Each victory progresses your 20‑level journey, unlocking new characters, deck designs, and card backs.

Progression and the Exiled Boss

Defeating the Exiled Boss unlocks a new map aboard the S.C. Defender, featuring reactive music, 150 unique scares, and a different entity. The cycle continues until level 20. You can defeat the Exiled Boss only five times to unlock the five hidden maps—each attempt harder than the last. Losing means returning to the table, winning a match, going back to the Prison, finding the four cards, and challenging the boss again for a new S.C. Defender room.

Menu → Lobby → Match (Victory) → Prison → Boss → New Map

Characters, cosmetics, and languages

The game includes 10 base characters, and through progression and cosmetics you can reach a total of 36 playable characters. With a Skull‑based economy and support for 44 languages, Memo R.I.P. blends psychological horror, strategy, and exploration into an experience that never repeats itself.

The game features 6 rooms, each containing 150 unique scares, for a total of 900 events that react to your Madness Bar. The higher it gets, the more vulnerable you become: you’ll see the entity that lives in the room, hear it, feel it, and fall for its distractions—forgetting your hand’s value and losing the match.

First‑person card gameplay

You play on cozy‑futuristic tables inside a spaceship, lit by stable or unstable neon depending on the room’s state. Each room has its own entity, its own behavior, and its own way of watching and manipulating you. You don’t know which one you’ll get. You don’t know which card will wake it up. You don’t know when it will move behind you.

Dynamic psychological horror

The Blackbell System alters the rules in real time. AI fills empty player slots. Vivox transmits your breathing, doubts, and reactions… but during Blackbell, you won’t hear your teammates—yet they will hear you. The six card‑game variants completely change the pace of each match.

The Exiled Prison

Winning a match is not the end. At certain levels, the trial of the Exiled Boss awaits: you wake up in the Exiled Prison, an explorable map inspired by PT, Visage, and Resident Evil. Find the Four Cards of Madness, solve puzzles, and survive the whispers trying to break your mind. Each victory progresses your 20‑level journey, unlocking new characters, deck designs, and card backs.

Progression and the Exiled Boss

Defeating the Exiled Boss unlocks a new map aboard the S.C. Defender, featuring reactive music, 150 unique scares, and a different entity. The cycle continues until level 20. You can defeat the Exiled Boss only five times to unlock the five hidden maps—each attempt harder than the last. Losing means returning to the table, winning a match, going back to the Prison, finding the four cards, and challenging the boss again for a new S.C. Defender room.

Menu → Lobby → Match (Victory) → Prison → Boss → New Map

Characters, cosmetics, and languages

The game includes 10 base characters, and through progression and cosmetics you can reach a total of 36 playable characters. With a Skull‑based economy and support for 44 languages, Memo R.I.P. blends psychological horror, strategy, and exploration into an experience that never repeats itself.

Penguin Rescue Run is a fast-paced 3D platformer focused on precision, reflexes, and challenging movement-based gameplay. Take control of a small penguin on a dangerous adventure to rescue his missing friend while overcoming deadly obstacles across a variety of themed environments.

Run, jump, and carefully navigate through levels filled with moving platforms, narrow paths, spinning hazards, traps, collapsing sections, and difficult precision jumps. Each stage introduces new platforming challenges that require timing, accuracy, and quick reactions to survive.

Explore multiple environments including frozen islands, desert ruins, floating sky arenas, and hazardous obstacle-filled courses. Collect coins scattered throughout the levels while attempting to reach the finish without falling.

As you progress, the difficulty gradually increases with more complex platform layouts, faster obstacles, riskier paths, and advanced movement challenges designed to test player skill and reflexes.

  • Stylized low-poly art style

  • Casual yet rewarding gameplay

  • Keyboard and controller support

  • Arcade-inspired obstacle course challenges

A dark-fantasy RPG about breaking the boundary between worlds... and surviving what comes through.

Veilbreak is a story-driven JRPG where reality itself is beginning to fracture. Across the land, ancient seals are failing... and something from beyond is pushing its way in.

What begins as a desperate escape from a cult ritual quickly spirals into a world on the brink of invasion. Portals tear open without warning. Creatures not meant for this world slip through, And somewhere beyond the Veil... something far worse is waiting.

You’ll lead a party of unlikely heroes- each pulled into a conflict far bigger than themselves. As the fractures spread, so does the truth:

This isn’t just an invasion.

It’s a search.

And you are being hunted.

Travel across coastal cities, ancient spires, underground trenches, and forgotten ruins as you track the source of the breaches. From the vibrant streets of Azura Bay to the depths of corrupted temples, every region brings new threats... and new answers.

Face twisted guardians, Veil-touched monstrosities, and powerful entities slipping between worlds. Close the fractures. Survive the encounters, and uncover why the barrier between realms is breaking... and who-or what-is trying to tear it down completely.

store_data.about_the_game:
Bench Simulator is a narrative simulation game where you experience the world from the perspective of a park bench.

Across several in-game days, different people come to the park, sit on the bench, and leave behind pieces of their lives. Couples, strangers, lonely night visitors, suspicious characters, families, and emotionally troubled people all pass through the same quiet place. You cannot walk, speak, or directly control them — but your small reactions can influence what happens.

As the bench, you observe conversations, read emotional situations, and react through subtle interactions such as shaking, shifting, creaking, or staying completely still. A small movement at the right time may interrupt an argument, create an awkward silence, comfort someone, or change the direction of a conversation.

Bench Simulator is not about action or combat. It is about presence, memory, timing, and the quiet impact of being there.

Every visitor brings a different story. Some moments are funny, some are romantic, some are uncomfortable, and some are emotionally heavy. As days pass, certain characters may return, previous choices may matter, and the bench slowly becomes a silent witness to the changing lives around it.

Key Features

- Play as a park bench in a unique narrative simulation experience

- Observe and influence conversations through subtle physical reactions

- Meet different visitors across multiple in-game days

- Experience emotional, funny, romantic, mysterious, and melancholic stories

- Make small choices that can affect character relationships and outcomes

- Discover recurring character arcs and different story consequences

- Experience day, evening, and night encounters with changing atmosphere

- Minimal, story-focused gameplay built around dialogue and observation

- Multiple outcome variations based on how you react during key moments

You are not the hero.

You are not the villain.

You are the bench.

You cannot speak.

You cannot leave.

But you can remember.

A missing girl. An endless nightmare. A detective who refuses to leave without her.

Story:

In 1982 detective Jackson Webb is sent to Investigate a missing persons report for Violet Blackthorne, a 19 year old run away, After retracing her last known location he is sent to an abandoned warehouse where after finding no trace of Violet noclips through the floor into a yellow office space that seems to go on forever.

Now faced with surviving and escaping his new predicament he finds traces of violet in these backrooms and is on a mission to bring himself and violet back home.

Gameplay:

Set in the multi levelled backrooms found in the wiki dot lore, you find yourself able to traverse multiple levels to find resources to survive, with a rare ability to noclip inside the backrooms transporting yourself into a private homebase for base building, item storage and a safe space to plan your next ventures into the depths of this infinite procedurally generated hellscape.

As a detective hell bent on bringing violet home you complete quests that lead you across all levels chasing any hint you can find about violets whereabouts, but be careful as you'll be battling and running away from all the entities hellbent on killing you first.

  • Survive procedurally generated backrooms while dealing with entities trying to kill you.

  • Juggle with your food, water and sanity while traversing different levels of backrooms lore.

  • Craft weapons and other tools to help aid in your survival.

  • Investigate clues that lead you to Violet.

store_data.about_the_game:
ABOUT THE GAME

The war ended an hour ago. The field is littered with bodies. Crows are already gathering. And you — just hungry teenagers from a nearby village trying to survive.

Welcome to Battlefield Rats — a cooperative medieval scavenger simulator where you and your friends loot fallen warriors, avoid dangers, and try to carry away as much treasure as possible without losing your life, sanity, or each other.

GAMEPLAY

Each nighttime raid is a tense mix of greed, fear, and chaos. Sneak across the battlefield, search knights’ and soldiers’ bodies, stuff your bags with armor, weapons, and coins. But remember: the more you carry, the slower you move, and every sound can attract unwanted attention.

Search fallen warriors for valuable loot, but be careful — not every body is truly dead.

Manage your fear: nervous characters drop items, scream, and can panic at the worst moments.

Avoid dangers: mounted patrols with torches, roaming deserters, packs of wild dogs, and something far worse stalk the field looking for scavengers like you.

Work as a team or betray your friends: share finds, cover each other’s escape, or abandon them to save yourself and your loot.

Return to the village alive: sell your haul, buy gear, feed your characters, and prepare for the next outing on even more dangerous fields.

KEY FEATURES

Co-op for 1-4 players with voice chat — coordinate, joke, or scream in terror together.

Unique characters with different abilities: a swift scout, skilled looter, strong carrier, or cautious observer.

Fear and nerves system: your characters respond to danger, and you’ll have to handle their panic.

Loot physics: items realistically clink, clang, and hamper movement — quietly hauling full armor won’t be easy.

Procedurally generated battlefields with varying dangers, weather, and combat types.

Meta-progression: develop your village, upgrade gear, unlock new fields, and complete special orders.

Unpredictable events: from comical (a crow steals your wallet) to horrifying (what you thought was a corpse suddenly grabs your leg).

WHO IS THIS GAME FOR

Battlefield Rats is made for groups of friends who love cooperative games with elements of horror and dark humor. If you enjoy Lethal Company, Content Warning, or Phasmophobia but want something with a historical setting and unique mechanics — this game is for you.

Get ready to laugh, scream, and betray your friends for a golden chain.

store_data.about_the_game:
CLICK YOURSELF INTO DAMNATION


Soul Clicker is an incremental clicker game about harvesting souls from the
depths of Hell. Start with a single click. End up running an infernal empire
that grinds out souls by the sextillion while you sleep.

Every soul you collect feeds a deeper, darker engine. Every prestige peels
back another layer. There is always a bigger number — and you will chase it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO


  • Click. A lot. Tap to earn souls. Buy buildings. Buy upgrades. Watch
    the numbers climb from 1 → 1,000 → 1 billion → 1 sextillion → and beyond.
  • Build an empire. 31 buildings across three tiers — base, advanced,
    and eternal. Each one produces souls automatically while you do other
    things. Stack them. Multiply them. Worship them.
  • Prestige. Forever. When you've climbed high enough, burn it all
    down for Prestige Points. Spend PP on 53 permanent upgrades across 8
    categories. Come back stronger. Climb faster. Burn it down again.
  • Master four realms. Each advanced building unlocks a minigame:
    • Chaos Engine — spend Chaos Orbs on a tree of building boosts
      and use them to buy Eternal Buildings outright.
    • Abyssal Drill — mine Ancient Fragments and roll for relics
      across five rarities and five effect types.
    • Soul Forge — gamble your souls. Win double or jackpot 10×.
      Lose them all.
    • Lust Labyrinth — hire workers who click for you while
      you're busy clicking for yourself.
  • Equip relics. Roll for randomized rarity-based gear. Stack
    Global CPS, Click power, cost reduction, and auto-clicks. Find the
    legendary All-Seeing Eye and watch every multiplier light up at once.
  • Chase 200+ achievements. Every one you unlock permanently
    boosts your soul production by 1%. By the time you've collected
    them all, idle income is nearly 4× stronger.

FEATURES


  • 31 buildings — from a single Tormented Soul to the Eternal Soul Nexus
  • 500+ building upgrades — each one a meaningful jump
  • 53 prestige upgrades across 8 themed categories
  • 4 fully-fleshed minigames tied to advanced buildings
  • 21 distinct relics across 5 rarities, with bulk inventory management
  • 200+ achievements — each one boosts CPS by 1%
  • 5 random events with massive temporary boosts
  • Custom soundtrack across three moods — pick Main, Lofi, or Metal
  • Independent SFX and BGM volume sliders
  • Save anywhere — local saves, plus export/import for backups
  • No microtransactions. No ads. No timers. No paywalls.

WHO IT'S FOR


If you've ever lost a weekend to Cookie Clicker, Adventure Capitalist, or
Antimatter Dimensions — Soul Clicker is for you. If the words "I'll just
prestige one more time" describe your relationship with games, this is
the abyss you've been looking for.

HOW LONG IS IT


Soul Clicker is endless. The first prestige takes about 30 minutes.
The first hundred prestiges take a couple of weeks. The achievement
hunters might still be playing six months from now.

You can play it actively, leave it running, or both. It rewards every
style.

Click. Build. Damn yourself.

store_data.about_the_game:
Relay Protocol is a logic-based puzzle game built around experimentation, spatial reasoning, and energy-based mechanics.

Play solo or with another player inside a mysterious industrial facility, using energy beams, reflective surfaces, logic devices, and environmental mechanisms to solve interconnected test chambers. Each player has a distinct role, and success depends on understanding how your actions affect your partner’s side of the puzzle.

Redirect lasers, activate surfaces, manipulate geometric signals, and coordinate timing-based interactions to progress deeper into the facility. Every room is built around clear rules, but the solutions require observation, experimentation, and teamwork.

Relay Protocol is designed for players who enjoy clean puzzle design, minimalistic sci-fi environments, and cooperative challenges where both players matter.

Features

  • Full campaign playable solo or in two-player co-op

  • Logic-based puzzle chambers built around experimentation and spatial reasoning

  • Energy beam mechanics with reflection, redirection, and signal transformation

  • Specialized units with distinct functions

  • Reactive surfaces, logic devices, and interconnected environmental mechanisms

  • Minimalistic industrial sci-fi atmosphere

  • Designed for players who enjoy clean puzzle design, discovery, and systemic problem solving

store_data.about_the_game:
Lys is fragmenting. Corrupted guardians protect what remains of the light — and they show no mercy.

SoulBound — Fragments of Lys is a cooperative action game for 1 to 4 players built around epic boss battles. Hard by design. Fair by principle. Impossible to put down once you start to understand.

The Challenge


Inspired by the souls-like philosophy, every guardian has readable patterns, learnable mechanics and an unforgiving margin for error. You will die. You will learn. And when you finally win, you will know exactly why.

Encounters are designed as miniature raids — with visual telegraphs, safe zones, DPS checks, phase transitions and an enrage state that completely transforms the boss's pattern. Two random players and four coordinated friends are entirely different experiences.

Weekly Affixes


Every weekly reset, the world changes. Global modifiers alter the rules of every encounter — forcing new strategies, new group compositions and a real reason to come back every week.

  • Enraged — all guardians start the encounter already in their enrage state
  • Deep Curse — debuffs last twice as long
  • Resurgence — guardians regenerate HP whenever they stop taking damage
  • Growing Abyss — the arena shrinks over time
  • Echo of Lys — each defeated guardian leaves a specter that repeats its deadliest attacks

Complete the weekly challenge before the reset to earn exclusive rewards.

Four Classes, Endless Combinations


Every class has exclusive 3-hit combos, unique abilities and an Ultimate that can turn lost battles around. In group play, class synergies unlock bonuses no solo player can achieve.

  • Warrior — absolute resilience, master of close-range combat
  • Mage — area spells and crowd control that redefine the battlefield
  • Healer — the group's foundation; without timing mastery, no one survives
  • Archer — ranged precision, target marking and tactical support

Progression


  • Skill Tree — permanent unlocks that change your playstyle, not just your numbers
  • Forge & Crafting — guardian materials become equipment that modifies abilities and combos
  • Per-Encounter Rankings — from Rank C to Rank S, every guardian has a score based on time and execution
  • Global Leaderboards — compare with players worldwide; in multiplayer, the board records the full group composition

Cooperative Multiplayer


  • Online co-op for up to 4 players via Steam
  • Dedicated server support
  • Guardian HP scales with player count
  • Group mechanics active only in co-op
  • Invite friends directly through the Steam overlay

store_data.about_the_game:
Storyline
You are hired to return to an abandoned circus shortly after it was shut down. Your task is simple: remove any evidence that could raise questions before investigators arrive. As you move through the empty tents and restricted areas, you begin to uncover signs that something went wrong. Objects left behind, locked sections of the circus, and scattered clues start to paint a picture you weren’t meant to see. It quickly becomes clear that you are not alone. Someone is still inside the circus… and they know you’re there.

Gameplay
The Incident is a first-person horror experience focused on exploration and environmental storytelling. Players will search the circus for evidence, interact with objects, and navigate through different areas to complete their objective. Gameplay revolves around exploring, collecting and destroying evidence, and avoiding the presence that remains within the circus. The game emphasizes atmosphere, building tension through sound, environment, and pacing rather than constant action. The experience is designed to be short and focused, with an estimated playtime of around 20–40 minutes.

store_data.about_the_game:
You inherit your grandfather's "Wanbao" banner and become the owner of a small shop.
Buy items brought in by customers, fill your shelves with goods, and sell them when someone shows interest—but that's just the beginning.
Repair damaged items, enhance equipment, and infuse them with "Star Power"… Each step can greatly increase an item's value—but watch both your wallet and your customers' purses.
Raise the name of "Wanbao" high, open chain stores across this fantasy world, and become a true business legend.

Use Suits & Ranks – Play the Psychological Game of Haggling

Real trading is never about the numbers on an abacus—it's a battle of hearts and minds! In this never‑ending "Merchant's Poker Game", you must find your own way.

  • Playing cards represent different negotiation attitudes:
    ♥️ Hearts = Emotion
    ♠️ Spades = Reason
    ♦️ Diamonds = Transaction
    ♣️ Clubs = Toughness
    The higher the number, the stronger the attitude – and they counter each other in a unique system.

  • 4 types of customers, each following their own logic of play.

Developer Note: Current version is a "Whitebox/Greybox" Test Build

The content on this page is primarily for collecting player feedback and iterative development. The current game visuals are in the whitebox (greybox) phase and do not represent the final art quality. We will adjust the gameplay based on player feedback, and we look forward to your valuable suggestions!

【Story Synopsis】

After the death of his beloved grandfather, the young grandson has been unable to accept this sorrow... To uncover the truth, he accidentally opens a gateway to the Underworld, and a thrilling adventure begins. Is death truly the end? And how should we perceive death?

【Core Gameplay】

CallBacker is a 3D top-down action-adventure game (Metroidvania). Players will control the protagonist to traverse various regions of the Underworld, defeating undead enemies through precise jumping and intense combat to find the way home.

【Game Features】

Fluid Combat System: Use a longsword to perform combos and utilize dodge mechanics to evade lethal attacks, experiencing a hardcore action feel.

Non-linear Map Exploration: The game features 5 distinct regions of the Underworld. You need to find special abilities to unlock new paths, explore hidden secret rooms, and experience the classic "ability-gated progression" fun.

Soul Ability Progression: As the adventure deepens, you can collect soul points to upgrade your health and attack power, or unlock new movement skills, such as double jump and dash.

Epic Boss Battles: Face 5 powerful Bosses guarding the depths of the Underworld, learn their attack patterns, defeat them, and obtain key items.

Heirs of the Moon is a survival adventure about legacy

Play as a wolf moving through an untamed world where every hunt matters and any mistake can mean death.

Heirs of the Moon features:

  • A perma-death system where once you die, you continue on as your pup. If there are no pups then your bloodline ends with you.

  • Intense emergent gameplay.

Survival is only the beginning. Form a pact, find a mate, and raise pups to carry your bloodline. Manage your pack and prepare for each outing with strategy.

Survive in an open world with a dynamic weather system across different terrains.

Each biome features different weather and different conditions. Adapt to the environment that you're in or risk your pack dying. Heirs of the Moon features 4 unique zones:

  • Marshlands

  • Snow mountain

  • Sand plains

  • Grassy plains

You need a pack to survive in this lonely world.
