store_data.about_the_game:
"Duel Mahjong" is an online multiplayer mahjong game incorporating item cards and superpowers. During matches, there are many ways to acquire item cards. By combining various card effects, you can devise winning strategies, enjoy a thrilling game of Mahjong with your friends!

Game features include:

Adding item cards to traditional Mahjong

  • The addition of item cards lowers the difficulty of building a winning hand. High-level winning hands are no longer just for show, making it easier to experience the thrill of winning big hands compared to traditional Mahjong.

  • The addition of item cards allows for greater operational and decision-making space, making the game more varied and increasing its fun and strategic depth.

  • With item cards, you can experience the fun of card games like combo skills, gambling, counter-attacks, and NTR (Netorare) within Mahjong.

Supports a certain degree of customizable Mahjong rules

  • In addition to many traditional Mahjong rule cards such as "fixed suit" and "ready hand," the game also includes various "battle" rule cards for expert players. You can DIY your favorite Mahjong rules by combining various rule cards.

  • The game includes over 120 Mahjong winning hands, and you can customize the winning hand table and the number of points.

  • The game includes over 200 item cards, and you can customize the card pool and the value of each card.

store_data.about_the_game:
Thick fog blankets the concrete residential blocks, and in the light of a lone streetlamp stands your "fortress" for the summer — an ordinary street kiosk. Uncle Alik has left on business, leaving behind a set of keys, a stack of paper invoices, and a pager. Your first night shift is ahead, and how it goes is entirely up to you.

This is an atmospheric vendor simulator set in the post-Soviet suburbs, where there is no place for rushing. Immerse yourself in the melancholic aesthetics of a bygone era: listen to the monotonous hum of an old refrigerator, count small change, and watch the night life of the foggy neighborhood unfold.

store_data.about_the_game:
YOU ARE A KIDNAPPING VICTIM

After a wild party with your coworkers, you wake up in the basement of an old castle — chained like an animal.
Darkness, occult symbols, and the remains of previous victims surround you. Why were you chosen?
Why did the cult single you out? Questions you don’t yet have answers to — and ones you must uncover yourself.

DECIDE YOUR FATE

Will you try to escape the Satanists' lair and find out why you were the victim? Will you save another victim… or only yourself? Or perhaps begin to see the cult from a different perspective? The choice is yours in Sacrificium

YOUR MENTALITY WILL BE TESTED

Every decision you make has consequences. What seems logical at first may lead to unexpected outcomes, and your choices will shape your fate. To survive in this cursed place, you'll have to do things you'd never normally consider — and some of those choices may slowly destroy your sanity. But you are not alone. The whisper in your ears keeps guiding you forward. Is it helping you survive... or have you already lost your mind?

FEATURES

⛧ Psychological horror with multiple endings.

⛧ An interactive text adventure set in the lair of Satanists.

⛧ Choices that affect sanity and health.

⛧ Atmospheric retro-inspired visuals.

⛧ Occult and satanic themes

store_data.about_the_game:
SINKING INTO THE VOID is a 2D side-scrolling hack-and-slash action game focused on intense battles against powerful enemies.

Players can equip up to three weapons at once and switch between them instantly to adapt to any situation.

Fast-paced combat combines movement, jumping, and dashing with melee attacks, ranged attacks, and abilities.

In addition to guarding enemy attacks, players can perform a precise “Just Guard (Parry)” by blocking at the exact right moment.

A successful parry can stun enemies, reflect projectiles, and completely turn the tide of battle.

Each stage features unique gimmicks and a wide variety of enemies, while boss stages offer even more challenging encounters.

The game also includes time attack elements, encouraging players to refine their routes, optimize their equipment, and push for faster clear times.

Equipment is divided into six slots: Right Hand, Left Hand, Head, Body, Arms, and Legs.

Items come in four rarity tiers: Normal, Rare, Epic, and Legend.

Equipment can also grant a wide range of special effects, such as:

  • Launching fireballs when attacking

  • Increasing damage as HP gets lower

  • Becoming invincible while jumping

By combining these effects, players can create their own unique combat style and build.

Carefully choosing randomly dropped equipment, refining builds, and constantly improving clear records are at the core of the experience.

SINKING INTO THE VOID is an action game designed to keep players saying, “Just one more run.”

【游戏特色】

📌 以“六艺”为骨，筑万象之基 游戏结构溯源中国古代君子必修的六门功课，构建出“礼、乐、射、御、书、数”六大主题卷宗。

  • 内容恢弘： 涵盖 36 大主题篇章，关卡纵贯古今中外。从历史地理到前沿理工，从诗词歌赋到流行影视，从体育竞技到动漫游戏，知识点无所不包。

  • 挑战升级： 每篇包含至少三个精心设计的填字残局。当你完成前六卷的洗礼，更有终极的第七卷“合”等待开启，挑战你知识储备的极限！

🧩 贴心交互，丝滑解谜体验 为了让玩家专注于思考而非操作，我们设计了极具人性化的辅助系统：

  • 视域聚焦： 当前选中的词条及其对应提示词将同步高亮显示，让你在密集的网格中瞬间锁定目标。

  • 词组连输： 全面支持各类中文输入法的词组连续输入！无需逐个选定方格，输入完整词条即可自动填充，让解谜如行云流水。

  • 温情助攻： 遇到暂时无法攻克的生僻字？点击“提示”按钮即可揭晓。

  • 一键校对： 拿不准填得对不对？随时使用“检查”功能，系统将即时反馈正确性，助你精准破局。

🎨 四季流转，定制视觉美学 游戏内置了“春、夏、秋、冬”四套独具匠心的视觉主题供你自由切换。

  • 从初春的淡绿竹影到凛冬的深邃静谧，每个主题都拥有专属的古典配色与 UI 细节。每一次点击，都如同在宣纸上翻阅一卷精美的水墨画册，让解谜过程成为视觉的享受。

🍃 沉浸式智力禅修 这里没有倒计时的焦虑，没有繁杂的操作负担。伴随着落笔时清脆悦耳的音效，看着错综复杂的网格被正确的字符填满。这不仅是解谜，更是一段属于你自己的、宁静且充满成就感的思维修行。

准备好接受“六艺”的洗礼了吗？落笔生花，就在此刻。

store_data.about_the_game:
Instead of a ball, cute fish bounce around and break blocks in this cozy idle block breaker. Rewards build up whenever fish hit blocks, and progress keeps growing inside a small aquarium on your screen.

The game is made to sit quietly at the side of your screen. While you work, watch videos, or play something else, fish keep bouncing, blocks keep breaking, and your run keeps growing in the small window.

A Little Aquarium Beside Your Screen

Different fish appear in the game, each with its own traits. Enjoy the rhythm as they bounce through the tank and break blocks. The mood is calm and low-pressure, like a tiny aquarium quietly moving next to your monitor.

Break Blocks and Grow

Fish bounce around, smash blocks, and earn rewards. Level up, strengthen skills, and grow so you can break more blocks faster. Simple rules meet idle progression, making even a quick check-in feel rewarding.

Treasures, Levels, and Skills

Lasers, symbols, and even jackpots! Collect different growth elements and shape your own path forward. Earn treasures, level up, strengthen skills, and improve the speed and efficiency of every block-breaking run. The longer the game stays open, the more growth choices you unlock.

Key Features

- A cozy idle block breaker you can keep open beside your screen, fish included

- Simple, intuitive block-breaking where fish with different traits take the place of the ball

- Rebirth growth that makes each cycle stronger than the last

- Treasures, levels, skills, and other upgrade elements

- Light progression built for quick check-ins or long idle sessions

- Supports both active play and idle play

store_data.about_the_game:
Giant Waifu Wash Simulator 💦 is a relaxing simulation game with sandbox and narrative elements, set in a bright coastal city where routine work can suddenly turn into something much more unusual.

You play as a professional cleaner, used to handling everyday tasks and keeping the streets spotless. But when a certain larger-than-life figure arrives without warning, your skills are put to the test in ways you never expected.

Take on a variety of satisfying cleaning jobs using specialized tools, explore a vibrant resort environment, and navigate a growing connection that doesn’t always follow a predictable path.

There’s no rush, no pressure — just you, your work, and whatever comes next.

✨ Key Features:

✨ Satisfying Cleaning Gameplay
Enjoy relaxing, detail-focused tasks designed to be both calming and rewarding.
💋 Unusual Encounters
Some jobs are bigger than others — and some leave a lasting impression.
😏 Subtle, Evolving Narrative
Your choices shape how things unfold, even when the full picture isn’t immediately clear.
🌴 Sunny Resort Atmosphere
A colorful, Miami-inspired setting full of life and contrast.
🔞 Mature-Themed Content
The experience includes suggestive scenarios and stylized interactions intended for an adult audience, presented in a non-explicit, atmospheric way.

store_data.about_the_game:
Arkada

A melancholic, quiet place where you came for one main purpose. . .
To play the arcades.

But the games will not let you get the victory so easily. You can lose yourself playing over and over, trying to prove that you are better while ignoring the passing time. Or you can take a walk, step away from the games, and listen to your thoughts as paranoia slowly takes over.

List of Games

Arkada -
  Play as a character interacting with the world most familiar to our

Illusionist -
  You play as a spirit orb encumbered in a forest. The creature watches you and bends the entire forest to make you perish. Dodge the forest’s grasp and keep hitting the creature to calm the forest.

Pirate Queen -
  Find which weapon is your favorite. Blast through hordes of enemies, collect fallen coins, and move through tight gaps as they close in on you. Find the legendary cave and claim the forsaken power. Don’t let them hit you. . . simple.

Glory -
  Race and drift against time on the roads, almost always at the maximum possible speed. And DO NOT STOP, neither willingly nor accidentally, otherwise you won't keep yourself alive.

Every path leads to a bitter blind end…

SURVIVE THE GALACTIC FRONTIER Welcome to Aethelgard. You are the commander of an upgradable starship lost in a hostile, resource-rich sector of deep space. Your mission is simple: mine rare ores, trade for powerful technology, and survive the endless waves of elite alien warships hunting you down.

UPGRADE YOUR ARSENAL Start with a basic vessel and transform it into an unstoppable dreadnought. Collect Kyberium and other precious resources from asteroid fields and defeated enemies to purchase devastating laser cannons, heavy shielding, and high-tech engine thrusters.

INTENSE SPACE COMBAT Experience fast-paced, top-down 2.5D space combat where positioning and strategy are everything. Dodge incoming enemy fire, launch calculated counter-attacks, and watch enemy ships explode in spectacular cinematic destruction.

  • Economy & Trading: Dock at space stations, access the Black Market, and carefully manage your credits.

  • Procedural Encounters: Face off against giant meteors, unexpected ambushes, and heavily armed alien bosses.

  • Cinematic 3D & 2.5D Atmosphere: Enjoy a breathtaking fully 3D environment played from a tactical 2.5D perspective. Marvel at moving starfields, deep space nebulas, dynamic 3D lighting, and stunning particle effects.

The sector is unforgiving. Will you become the ultimate Galactic Guardian?

store_data.about_the_game:
Paint pixels. Watch chaos unfold.

Pixel Rain is a relaxing falling-sand physics sandbox where every cell on a giant grid obeys its own rules. Pour water, drop sand, ignite lava, grow crystals — then sit back and watch it all interact.

There's no campaign, no fail state, no pressure. Just you, a canvas full of physics-driven pixels, and a lot of satisfying emergent behaviour.

Hundreds of Materials to Paint With

  • Sand — piles and settles naturally

  • Water — flows, pools, and reacts with almost everything

  • Lava — turns water into steam, melts ice, ignites everything nearby

  • Acid — slowly corrodes stone, metal, and crystal

  • Oil — floats on water, highly flammable

  • Crystal — grows from water and ice into spreading formations

  • Plant — feeds on water and spreads organically

  • Plasma — decays into sparks over time

  • Void — silently erases everything it touches

  • Magnet — pulls nearby metal cells toward it

  • Plus: Paint, Slime, Foam, Snow, Ice, Smoke, Spark, Stone, Metal

  • …and 400+ more — from concrete, salt and sawdust to charged crystal, living wood and brimstone. Combine any two materials and you might discover a brand-new one.

Features

  • 60 FPS physics simulation on a dynamic grid up to ~620×480 cells

  • 400+ paintable materials and brush presets with scatter, sparkle, and jitter tuning

  • 6 customizable quick-slot brushes

  • Adjustable gravity, flow speed, brush size, and zoom

  • 3 procedurally synthesized music modes: Rain, Magma, and Aurora

  • Procedural sound effects keyed to each material — no audio files, all generated in real time

  • One-button MP4 clip export (R to record, R to save)

  • Showcase cinematic mode (T) — the camera finds the most active region of your canvas and records it automatically

  • Save and load your canvas, synced across devices with Steam Cloud

  • 100+ Steam achievements with progress bars and in-game toasts

  • 50+ discoverable recipes — combine two materials to alchemize a third

  • Steam Workshop — design your own materials, brushes and animations with built-in editors (plus a DevMode code editor), then share them and subscribe to community creations

  • Built-in tutorial to get you started

  • Custom color palette and lobby theming

Early Access

Pixel Rain is in Early Access. The core simulation is fully playable and stable. Expect new materials, brush tools, and quality-of-life improvements as development continues. Feedback welcome.

In the depths of a forgotten cave, far from any light, a man awakens amidst blood, stone, and corpses.
Betrayed by the one he once called his companion in fortune, abandoned to the darkness like just another body left to rot, only one thing now drives him forward: vengeance.

But the world awaiting him beyond this stone tomb is no longer human.

Ruined kingdoms, villages consumed by madness, grotesque creatures, fanatical cults, and cursed lands form the remnants of a dark fantasy world on the brink of collapse. Everywhere, despair devours the living as much as the dead. Every path seems to lead deeper into suffering, decay, and fear.

In VERLIES III - Resurrection, explore oppressive dungeons, face monstrous enemies, and survive intense rhythmic combat where every strike, dodge, and mistake may seal your fate. Progress through a brutal interconnected world, uncover the secrets of a dying civilization, and relentlessly hunt the one who condemned you.

For some betrayals deserve worse than death.

THE DEALER'S STRATEGY: MANAGE YOUR FORTUNE

In Die Die, your deck isn't just a pile of cards—it's your dynamic loadout. Master a unique 5-slot inventory system to survive:

  • The Weapon (1 Slot): Your primary tool for destruction.

  • Passive Traits (3 Slots): Stack stats and unique abilities to define your build.

  • The Active Card (1 Slot): Your tactical ace. Use it to heal, clear the screen of bullets, or save a powerful card for later.

KEY FEATURES:

  • Strike for Luck: Cards aren't free. Attack enemies to generate Luck, the essential resource needed to draw from your deck.

  • The Empty Deck Threat: If you run out of cards, you're back to basics. Without your deck, you'll be forced to fight with a weak starter weapon.

store_data.about_the_game:
When the world needs a cure by August, every promise becomes a liability—and every connection becomes a choice.

In Hanta Hearts, you are Holt, the CEO of a Cambridge biotech racing a twelve-week countdown to file an emergency-use authorization for AL-447, the only promising antibody against a fast-spreading hantavirus outbreak. Your days are measured in board calls, agency frameworks, manufacturing deviations, and contracts signed under fluorescent light—until three formidable women step into the same calendar, each with a different stake in the crisis. Choose one Saturday, and you choose the relationship that will shape the filing, the fallout, and what you're willing to risk.

Meet the Cast




Linnea — "The Exposure"
General Counsel for the cruise line at the center of the outbreak, Linnea arrives with a $48M pre-purchase agreement in one hand and eleven class actions in the other. She and Holt aren't just negotiating supply—they're negotiating risk, leverage, and what becomes discoverable when the world starts suing.



Verity — "The Indication"
An FDA Division Director writing the very framework AL-447 must file under, Verity is authority made human—precise, conditional, and famously difficult to sway. Holt meets her across the table where careers and public health intersect, and the attraction that builds is shadowed by ethics rules and scrutiny.



Hadley — "The Molecule"
Aletheia's Chief Scientific Officer and the inventor of record on AL-447, Hadley is the mind behind the science everyone will cite when the outcome matters. She's Holt's most essential ally inside the company—brilliant, exacting, and quietly aware that having her name on every page of the filing makes her both indispensable and replaceable.

Key Features


  • A high-stakes, modern thriller-romance set inside biotech and federal oversight
  • Single-choice branching romance structure: one decisive weekend splits the story into three distinct routes
  • Three love interests, three power dynamics: the inventor, the regulator, and the general counsel
  • 9 adult scenes across three romance routes
  • A complete seasonal arc with decisive resolutions

Content


Hanta Hearts is an adult romance visual novel. Each romance route includes explicit adult scenes. Contains strong language and mature themes including public health crisis pressure, legal conflict, and workplace power dynamics.

The Last Braincell: Escape is a humorous, asymmetrical multiplayer game in which one player takes on the role of the fugitive, while the others cooperate as the police. The fugitive tries to gather resources, conceal their identity, and reach the escape point, while the officers collect clues, search the area, and coordinate the pursuit.

Main characters:

Fugitive (Orange Braincell)

Clever, chaotic, and definitely way too confident. His goal is to disappear off the map, secure a fake identity, and reach the escape point before the police cut off every possible route. He can improvise, hide in absurd places, and pull off ideas that sound terrible on paper but somehow work.

Police Officer (Blue Braincell)

Alert, stubborn, and fully prepared to search half the map over a single suspicious report. He operates based on clues, tips from civilians, and coordination with other officers. He must quickly assess situations, secure areas, and anticipate the fugitive’s moves before he vanishes across the border. 

Goals in the game :

Prototype build. Release date: TBD. Wishlist now!

store_data.about_the_game:
Sticks and Stones is a post-apocalyptic survival simulator set after an asteroid (or asteroids) impact.
Other cataclysms might be added over time, but they will always involve massive, global-scale destruction.

1. What happens before you start the game?

The Iron Rock Corporation builds hundreds of shelters for millionaires - the chosen few who will have a chance to survive the destruction of the planet.

Shelter "Iron Rock 404" is currently under construction, just a few months away from completion.
Security systems are being installed, and supplies are being stockpiled to sustain over a hundred people for at least 36 months.

But an asteroid is about to hit the Earth (one massive impact or several smaller ones) - sooner than everyone expected.
Luckily - for you - you just happened to be nearby Iron Rock 404.

2. No two games will be the same.

Installed systems (including the AI managing the shelter), delivered equipment, seeds/seedlings, food, water, crafting materials, gas/fuel, medicine, clothing, weapons, etc. 
Available items are shaped by earlier deliveries (and sometimes by mistake), offering different resource ratios each game. 
Just like the meteorite impact itself, this creates a completely new challenge for the player in every single game.

3. You - the Hero.

When creating your character, you can either build one from scratch or choose one of several specialized presets with fixed attributes:

  • Shelter Mayor: As useless as humanly possible. Always carries a pistol but has terrible aim. Zero skills, but he is the only character with access keys to every room - including those that are otherwise impossible to open.
    (Though depending on the asteroid impact, the walls of these rooms might collapse, making their contents accessible even if you aren't the Mayor).

  • Head of Security: Zero practical skills, but massive theoretical knowledge. Read and watched a lot on the job but never actually did anything. Always starts with a weapon (not necessarily a pistol) and knows how to use it.

  • IT Specialist: Like the Mayor, physically useless, but high IQ, and holds full system access. Can unlock every AI function or shut the AI down without much hassle. Survival, farming, and physical fitness skills are practically zero.

  • Construction Worker: Strong, fit, averagely intelligent, but can fix anything, craft many items, and always comes with one random extra perk (farming, survival, amateur chemist, etc.).

  • Farmer: Hired to deliver and process the shelter's food stockpiles. Huge knowledge of crops (both practical and theoretical). Sometimes gets extra perks at the cost of slightly lower farming skills.

  • Warehouse Worker: The only character capable of operating forklifts and other warehouse equipment.
    Good at fixing machinery, an avid hunter and weekend trekker, and grows a home garden.
    And he is a smoker - he really (REALLY!) needs cigarettes.

3.1. Custom Character

Creating a custom character lets you tailor the protagonist to your exact preferences, though certain abilities will be capped.

4. Game Start - The First Impact.

An asteroid (or asteroids) is about to hit Earth.

Once the seismic tremors stop, the AI reboots and runs a damage assessment. If any of the three communication links (cable, radio or satellite) reconnects with the company's main server and/or NASA, the AI will pull data on the destruction, provide a estimated (ETA) for the shockwave, and plan your next steps.

5. Time.

Time passes at different rates:

  • x3 when in a safe area (any shelter, tent, igloo, or outdoor shelter).

  • x6 - x60 when outside safe zones (e.g., wandering the wasteland, exploring ruined towns).

  • Performing complex tasks (reading, cooking, repairing, crafting) or sleeping advances time by a set amount specific to that action.

Important!

Sticks and Stones is a realistic simulator: there is no classic HUD, including an on-screen clock.
You check the time by looking at a watch (if you have a working one) or via the terminal (if the power is on, it works, and the AI isn't currently planning your demise - see point 16. AI).
Time isn't just hours and minutes; days matter too (see point 14. Everything is relative).

Sound works similarly. Aside from bodily status notifications ("you feel cold," "you lost feeling in your left foot," "your backpack feels lighter"), there are no UI sounds. You only hear ambient noises, machinery, the AI voice, footsteps etc.
You'll hear an item drop on concrete.  You won't hear it drop on snow during a blizzard.
If you find a working music player, you can always listen to tunes.

6. Aftermath.

Once the immediate threats (tremors, shockwaves) pass, going outside remains impossible due to extreme heat, fires, falling debris, and hurricane winds - unless you have specialized hazmat gear.
This lockdown lasts from a few days to several weeks, depending on the impact severity.

7. Inventory Check.

Your first major task is assessing available supplies.
The easiest method is scanning all products for the AI to analyze.
(Unless you're the Warehouse Worker, you probably don't know how to use the scanner, but there's a manual lying around somewhere).
Input the number of residents (just you, so "1"), and the AI calculates how long supplies will last based on your diet (eating to your heart's content, strict bare-minimum rationing. etc.).

You might hit the jackpot and find the full 36-month stockpile for 100+ people delivered intact - securing your survival for a very long time.

But... When it turns out you have massive stockpiles of fresh food early on, or an amazing harvest (see point 10. Farming), most of it might rot before you can eat it.

8. Cooking, Processing, and Storage.

Some foods will make you sick if eaten raw; others just taste worse or spoil quickly.
You have access to a gas and electric stove, microwave, dehydrator, and freeze-dryer.
You'll find appliance manuals and cookbooks scattered around.
You can also freeze food if the freezer works and has free space inside.

Important!

Eating takes time. A normal meal takes about 5 minutes, but a delicious one vanishes in 2–3 minutes.
Conversely, if you dump a hell of a lot of salt into your soup, you might sit there for 10 minutes, barely force down a few spoons, and suffer side effects.

Speaking of food...

9. What goes in, must come out.

Physiology is part of the game.
Whatever you eat or drink, most of it eventually leaves your body - front or back, top or bottom.
Inside the shelter, it's fine (toilets on every floor). But on long expeditions, especially in freezing cold or irradiated zones, taking off your hazmat suit has severe consequences.

10. Farming.

To survive, you need to eat. You can't buy food - you must grow it.

Stockpiles buy you weeks, but crops need time to grow.

You have growboxes - assuming they arrived on time - to quickly grow veggies and fruits.

You just need seeds, water, power, a few supplies, and the know-how.

If the growboxes didn't arrive or broke and you can't fix them, use the old-school pre-apoc method your parents or grandparents used: dump soil on a room floor or into containers and plant away.

11. Water.

If the surface isn't irradiated (it likely is), you have endless snow to melt.

Luckily, water inside the shelter doesn't magically disappear; it changes form into food moisture, sewage, or humidity. (By the way, humidity is your worst enemy in a sealed reinforced concrete bunker... black mold).

If water stocks drop, set up water reclamation.

12. Energy.

Energy is critical. Gas and diesel run out fast.
Thick clouds block the sun, leaving two options:

  • a wind farm (which acts as a beacon for bandits)

  • or scavenging runs.

13. Expeditions.

You can go on short runs to nearby ruins for loot: canned beans, painkillers, coal, maybe a jerrycan of fuel.
Ignore cash, gold, or jewelry - they are worthless. Food and meds are the new currency.

13.1 Short runs require just a warm clothes and a sled.

13.2 Long expeditions are a massive challenge. You need enough food and water for the whole trip (you might find nothing), a weapon (encounters won't be friendly), and a first-aid kit.
Shelter is paramount. You might find an intact bunker in the ruins, or you might walk the wasteland for days, so..
A tent is a must-have for any long expeditions - especially if you get lost.

14. Everything is relative.

In Sticks and Stones, everything is relative.
No watch? You don't know the time.
No calendar and the AI fails? You don't know the date, meaning you don't know if food/meds are fresh or expired and poisonous.

The map works the same way.
You must physically possess a map (found or draw one).
Your position on it is relative - it's only accurate if you actually know where you are (e.g. standing next to a known landmark like the bunker, a specific building, canyon, or mountain).
Otherwise, it relies entirely on your survival / orienteering skills.
High skills = accurate map marker.
Low skills = wrong position and - worse - wrong directional facing.
Until you level up those skills, stick to known routes or leave markers on the ground, or you become frozen food for bandits.

15. Crafting Clothing and Equipment.

Like cooking, crafting and repairing gear requires knowledge and raw materials.
Scavenge materials via recycling items found in the shelter or on runs.
Or craft your own textiles and spare parts.

14.1 In Sticks and Stones, you cannot craft a gun out of a piece of wood and a spam can.
Crafting even the simplest firearm (highly rare guarantees of safety) requires immense skill.
Producing complex guns or ammo (especially primers) requires master-level skills, extensive tooling, and incredibly scarce materials impossible to manufacture post-apocalypse.

16. AI.

The pinnacle of pre-disaster human achievement will help you manage the shelter early on.
The AI automates many tasks, heavily easing the early game.
But... it has one major flaw: just like you, it wants to survive.
If power levels drop critical, the AI will treat you as the primary threat, and... dangerous, weird things will start happening. You have two choices: secure enough power, or pull the plug on the AI. Neither is easy.

17. Early Access

A Kickstarter campaign is launching soon, dictating the Early Access release date.
I'm tentatively planning Early Access around version 0.6 or 0.7.
If the Kickstarter succeeds, backers get access starting at version 0.3.

18. Roadmap / Release Schedule.

  • Version 0.3 (September or October 2026)
    Book learning, warehouse management, farming, and cooking a dozen or so meals.

  • Version 0.4 (November or December 2026)
    Crafting everyday items, recycling, side effects/diseases, and medical treatment.

  • Version 0.5 (January or February 2027)
    Expeditions to nearby towns/villages, item repairs, basic degradation (clothes, tools), and bodily injuries (cuts, fractures, frostbite).

  • Version 0.6 (March or April 2027)
    Advanced crafting (weapons, fertilizers, specialized gear, tents), and longer expeditions.

  • Version 0.7 (May or June 2027)
    Less aggressive enemies (muggers who rob rather than kill) and combat system. Small shelters in towns/villages with better loot.

  • Version 0.8 (July or August 2027)
    Aggressive, lethal, cannibalistic enemies. Drastic medical procedures (e.g., amputation for severe infection or frostbite).

  • Version 0.9 (September or October 2027)
    Mostly visual polish - more clothes, everyday items, plus highly requested quality-of-life items I might have missed.

  • Version 1.0 (November or December 2027)
    Full Release, with a few surprises thrown in for good measure.

You might hit the jackpot and find the full 36-month stockpile for 100+ people delivered intact - securing your survival for a very long time.

But... When it turns out you have massive stockpiles of fresh food early on, or an amazing harvest (see point 10. Farming), most of it might rot before you can eat it.

8. Cooking, Processing, and Storage.

Some foods will make you sick if eaten raw; others just taste worse or spoil quickly.
You have access to a gas and electric stove, microwave, dehydrator, and freeze-dryer.
You'll find appliance manuals and cookbooks scattered around.
You can also freeze food if the freezer works and has free space inside.

Important!

Eating takes time. A normal meal takes about 5 minutes, but a delicious one vanishes in 2–3 minutes.
Conversely, if you dump a hell of a lot of salt into your soup, you might sit there for 10 minutes, barely force down a few spoons, and suffer side effects.

Speaking of food...

9. What goes in, must come out.

Physiology is part of the game.
Whatever you eat or drink, most of it eventually leaves your body - front or back, top or bottom.
Inside the shelter, it's fine (toilets on every floor). But on long expeditions, especially in freezing cold or irradiated zones, taking off your hazmat suit has severe consequences.

10. Farming.

To survive, you need to eat. You can't buy food - you must grow it.

Stockpiles buy you weeks, but crops need time to grow.

You have growboxes - assuming they arrived on time - to quickly grow veggies and fruits.

You just need seeds, water, power, a few supplies, and the know-how.

If the growboxes didn't arrive or broke and you can't fix them, use the old-school pre-apoc method your parents or grandparents used: dump soil on a room floor or into containers and plant away.

11. Water.

If the surface isn't irradiated (it likely is), you have endless snow to melt.

Luckily, water inside the shelter doesn't magically disappear; it changes form into food moisture, sewage, or humidity. (By the way, humidity is your worst enemy in a sealed reinforced concrete bunker... black mold).

If water stocks drop, set up water reclamation.

12. Energy.

Energy is critical. Gas and diesel run out fast.
Thick clouds block the sun, leaving two options:

  • a wind farm (which acts as a beacon for bandits)

  • or scavenging runs.

13. Expeditions.

You can go on short runs to nearby ruins for loot: canned beans, painkillers, coal, maybe a jerrycan of fuel.
Ignore cash, gold, or jewelry - they are worthless. Food and meds are the new currency.

13.1 Short runs require just a warm clothes and a sled.

13.2 Long expeditions are a massive challenge. You need enough food and water for the whole trip (you might find nothing), a weapon (encounters won't be friendly), and a first-aid kit.
Shelter is paramount. You might find an intact bunker in the ruins, or you might walk the wasteland for days, so..
A tent is a must-have for any long expeditions - especially if you get lost.

14. Everything is relative.

In Sticks and Stones, everything is relative.
No watch? You don't know the time.
No calendar and the AI fails? You don't know the date, meaning you don't know if food/meds are fresh or expired and poisonous.

The map works the same way.
You must physically possess a map (found or draw one).
Your position on it is relative - it's only accurate if you actually know where you are (e.g. standing next to a known landmark like the bunker, a specific building, canyon, or mountain).
Otherwise, it relies entirely on your survival / orienteering skills.
High skills = accurate map marker.
Low skills = wrong position and - worse - wrong directional facing.
Until you level up those skills, stick to known routes or leave markers on the ground, or you become frozen food for bandits.

15. Crafting Clothing and Equipment.

Like cooking, crafting and repairing gear requires knowledge and raw materials.
Scavenge materials via recycling items found in the shelter or on runs.
Or craft your own textiles and spare parts.

14.1 In Sticks and Stones, you cannot craft a gun out of a piece of wood and a spam can.
Crafting even the simplest firearm (highly rare guarantees of safety) requires immense skill.
Producing complex guns or ammo (especially primers) requires master-level skills, extensive tooling, and incredibly scarce materials impossible to manufacture post-apocalypse.

16. AI.

The pinnacle of pre-disaster human achievement will help you manage the shelter early on.
The AI automates many tasks, heavily easing the early game.
But... it has one major flaw: just like you, it wants to survive.
If power levels drop critical, the AI will treat you as the primary threat, and... dangerous, weird things will start happening. You have two choices: secure enough power, or pull the plug on the AI. Neither is easy.

17. Early Access

A Kickstarter campaign is launching soon, dictating the Early Access release date.
I'm tentatively planning Early Access around version 0.6 or 0.7.
If the Kickstarter succeeds, backers get access starting at version 0.3.

18. Roadmap / Release Schedule.

  • Version 0.3 (September or October 2026)
    Book learning, warehouse management, farming, and cooking a dozen or so meals.

  • Version 0.4 (November or December 2026)
    Crafting everyday items, recycling, side effects/diseases, and medical treatment.

  • Version 0.5 (January or February 2027)
    Expeditions to nearby towns/villages, item repairs, basic degradation (clothes, tools), and bodily injuries (cuts, fractures, frostbite).

  • Version 0.6 (March or April 2027)
    Advanced crafting (weapons, fertilizers, specialized gear, tents), and longer expeditions.

  • Version 0.7 (May or June 2027)
    Less aggressive enemies (muggers who rob rather than kill) and combat system. Small shelters in towns/villages with better loot.

  • Version 0.8 (July or August 2027)
    Aggressive, lethal, cannibalistic enemies. Drastic medical procedures (e.g., amputation for severe infection or frostbite).

  • Version 0.9 (September or October 2027)
    Mostly visual polish - more clothes, everyday items, plus highly requested quality-of-life items I might have missed.

  • Version 1.0 (November or December 2027)
    Full Release, with a few surprises thrown in for good measure.

store_data.about_the_game:
Maybe it's money, maybe it's glory, maybe it's something else... you aren't exactly sure. But an overwhelming urge drives you straight into that dungeon.

Incremental Quest - Dungeon Depths

Blending the chill experience of a casual idle game with a gritty dark fantasy rpg atmosphere, Incremental Quest - Dungeon Depths is a modern take on old-school PC role-playing games.

Take on the role of an adventurer who has little to lose and everything to gain from "The Dungeon."

Descend deeper, grow stronger, and build your perfect setup to conquer every floor in an incremental loop designed to immerse you in that classic RPG flair.

Auto-Battling

Once you enter The Dungeon, combat happens automatically as you clash with any monster that crosses your path.

Training Grounds

To survive the deeper levels of The Dungeon, you must grow stronger. You can train attack and defense back in The City... for a price, of course.

The Craftsmith

Gear is vital for survival. Spend your hard-earned gold in The City to upgrade your equipment for the next descent.

Loot & Drops

The City's Craftsmith isn't the only place to find gear. The most powerful and rarest items are claimed directly from the enemies you defeat.

From the developer

You can subscribe to the waitlist to get updates on the game's progress.
Thank you for following my development journey, thank you for wishlisting, and most of all, thank you for your time.

store_data.about_the_game:
Idlemoor is a dark fantasy idle RPG set in a persistent online realm of ruined settlements, grim barrows, and slow-burning character growth.

Choose how your character survives: fight enemies, train combat styles, gather resources, craft gear, trade with other players, fight against other players in PvP, and climb the rankings. Progress continues while you are away, but active players can make sharper decisions, react to community events & random events, manage the market, and push deeper into the world.

Core Features

Persistent online progression
Your character keeps advancing over time through server-side saves and account-based progress.

Combat, training, gathering, and PvP battlegrounds
Fight players & creatures, improve combat stats, mine, woodcut, forage, skin animals, and build your character through multiple highly-connected complex gear & stat systems! 

Player economy
Buy, sell, and trade through a shared marketplace where player activity shapes item movement.  Each item is totally unique, and will never drop with identical stats.  Build your character with multiple in-depth skill systems, as well as several stat and gear systems that connect to form a complex meta-game of infinite potential choices!

Community features
Chat with other players, compete on rankings, engage in community events every day, and take part in a persistent realm instead of a purely local idle game.

Idle Pacing
Idlemoor is built for long-term progression: short check-ins, longer grinds, rare drops, and slow accumulation of power.

store_data.about_the_game:
Spin. Win. Collect. Repeat.

Reel Greed is a slot machine incremental where every win turns into a shower of physical money pickups. Start with tiny payouts, collect every bill you can, and build a machine that grows faster, stronger, and more ridiculous with every upgrade.

Each run gives you new chances to improve your setup. Pick powerful run cards, unlock permanent upgrades, increase your payouts, speed up the reels, and turn small wins into room-filling cash explosions.

The more you play, the more the machine changes. Spins get faster. Rewards get bigger. Coins unlock new paths. Cards create temporary power spikes. Before long, a few harmless payouts can turn into a chaotic pile of money covering the screen.

From Pocket Change to Ridiculous Wealth

Every run gives you new ways to scale:

- Increase starting chips, bet value, and payout multipliers

- Unlock new patterns and stronger upgrade paths

- Pick run cards that boost your current or next run

- Improve coin drops, collection range, and spin speed

- Build combinations that turn simple wins into huge payouts

- Watch money pile up, fade, and get collected

Features

- Money and coin pickups that fall, pile up, and flood the screen

- Permanent upgrade tree with branching paths

- Run cards that create short-term build choices

- Pattern-based slot payouts with scaling multipliers

- Fast, satisfying incremental progression

- Chaotic money explosions from big wins

- Short-session friendly, with plenty of room to keep pushing further

store_data.about_the_game:
Vector Storm is a fast-paced top-down arcade shooter that rewards aggression, precision, and smart builds.

Fight through endless waves of escalating enemies, survive devastating boss encounters, and grow stronger with every

run.

Survive. Build. Repeat.

Each run drops you into an arena that gets deadlier by the wave. Clear enemies to earn credits, spend them in the

mid-run shop on weapons and upgrades, and scavenge gear from fallen bosses. Die, bank your tokens, and come back

stronger.

Build Your Loadout

Equip tiered gear across seven slots — cockpit, wings, boosters, plating, shield, dampener, and weapon bay. Every

piece changes how your ship performs. Stack synergies, push your combo multiplier, and find the build that carries you

deepest.

Five Ships. Five Playstyles.

Start with the balanced Viper or unlock faster, stranger ships as you clear waves. The heavy Bastion regenerates

shields. The Phantom opens with a stealth window. The Ironclad reflects damage back. Each ship demands a different

approach.

Meta-Progression

Tokens earned each run fund permanent upgrades — more health, faster fire rate, bonus starting credits, and more. Sink

enough tokens into the tree and the arena changes with you.

Features

[] Endless wave-based survival with escalating difficulty

[] Seven-slot gear system with tiered boss drops

[] Five unlockable ships with unique passives

[] Deep mid-run upgrade shop

[] Persistent meta-progression across runs

[] Multiple distinct boss encounters

[] 44 Steam achievements

[] Global leaderboards

[*] Procedurally generated adaptive soundtrack

Storm City is drowning in crime and corruption. The streets belong to violent gangs, corporate interests, and anyone with enough firepower to take what they want.

The old ways failed.

So justice answered with a roar.

You are the Sentinel. Storm City’s first cybernetic law enforcer, built to restore order by any means necessary.

The Sentinel is built to take punishment, but survival depends on controlling the chaos around you. Break enemy morale, make arrests under pressure, rescue civilians caught in the crossfire and decide who gets taken alive or faces Zero Tolerance.

The Sentinel was built for more than destruction. Rescue loyal citizens caught in the chaos, identify real threats and avoid unnecessary casualties while restoring order.

store_data.about_the_game:
Exhibition of the Heart is a yuri visual novel about love, exhibitionism, and being true to your heart. 

It features 14 beautiful pieces of CG art and a story of ~70,000 words. 

This is a kinetic visual novel, so the reader does not have to make any choices and can simply enjoy the cute and lewd yuri story.

Alice is a girl who, in her own words, has no special talents and absolutely no potential to succeed in life. She graduated high-school without ever confessing to her crush, the seemingly perfect gifted genius Sylvia. In the three years that passed since graduation, she never got over or moved past that first love of hers. 

That is until, one day, she returned to her sleepy hometown for summer vacation. While taking a walk in the woods, she discovered her old crush Sylvia masturbating out deep in the bush! She couldn't believe that the serious and studious girl she had a crush on, had grown up into a shameless exhibitionist! 

Sylvia confronts Alice after being caught, and confesses that she has a secret fetish for doing it in public spaces without being seen, and that she has always wanted to try it in public with another girl. At first Alice is shocked by Sylvia's strange fetish, but vows to transform herself into an exhibitionist to impress her, and asks Sylvia to train her in the ways of lesbian exhibitionism. 

Can the timid and shy Alice push past her fear of getting caught and win Sylvia's heart? Find out in this lewd and cute yuri visual novel!

store_data.about_the_game:
Earth has been ravaged by a nuclear catastrophe. For 150 years, the descendants of the last survivors have drifted through space aboard the 'Ark'. Now, at this critical juncture, food supplies are dwindling, and seeds of distrust have begun to sprout among the people. Maintaining provisions, order, and cohesion has become your paramount mission.

Can you and the other 500 crew members endure the journey and keep the flame of humanity alive?

You must address the Ark's needs and resolve the dilemmas faced by your crew.

Game Features:

Seven experts are on an adventure with you, from left to right: Space Observer Jessica, Farmer Max, Researcher Karen, Coach Abigail, Clerk Zoe, Programmer Sakura, and Security Guard Ray.

Overcome crises:

Within 30 days, you must fulfill the needs aboard the Ark and help the crew resolve their hardships.

Each day on the ship is divided into two parts: routine actions and unexpected events. The core gameplay revolves around using the resources gathered from your daily actions to resolve these events.

Multiple endings：

The game offers 26 endings (A-Z) and branching storylines, where your choices will determine the fate of humanity aboard the 'Ark'!

Unlock abilities：

Unlock different abilities and decision branches, growing stronger with each challenge!

A vast background story and extensive data (databases, observation rooms) await your exploration!

store_data.about_the_game:
MyBiz — A Cozy Office, Run on Pomodoros

Build the most charming office on the block while you actually get work done. MyBiz is a desktop companion that turns your real focus sessions into in-game progress — every keystroke, every click, every Pomodoro funds a tiny pixel-art business that grows alongside your day.

How it works

Start a 25-minute Pomodoro and the office comes alive. Your typing fills a Keys bar, your clicks fill a Clicks bar, your music fills a Music bar — hit thresholds, earn cash and XP, level up, hire staff, expand to new floors. Take a break and the timer mode swaps to short or long break automatically. Skip out early? You still get prorated rewards.

Key features

  • Pomodoro that pays you back — 25/5/15 cycles tracked across the day, with cash and XP rewards calibrated so a single focused session feels meaningful.

  • Build a working office — buy desks, chairs, plants, lamps, recreation. Each piece of decor boosts staff output. Renovate floors (1F → 2F → 3F+), swap walls, doors, stairs, flooring.

  • Hire a team — staff sit at their desks and add passive bonus rewards to every Pomodoro you run. Each one costs a daily salary though, so growing your office means balancing payroll against output. Watch them work while you work.

  • Keep them happy — every staffer has a personal mood bar that slowly decays. Music, fresh decor, and shared coin grabs lift it back up. Happier teams output more — and play better at the foosball table on breaks

  • Customize your character — hair, hat, top, bottom, shoes — earned or bought, swap anytime.


Tools that help you focus

  • Music player — built-in playlist across Pop, R&B, Lo-fi, Jazz, Classic, Bossa, Funk. Auto-advance through the queue, loop the playlist, drop in your own tracks.

  • Ambience mixer — rain, forest, ocean, fireplace, wind, whatever puts you in the zone. Layer multiple sounds with individual volumes; resumes automatically next time you launch.

  • Quick tools — sticky notes, to-do list, clipboard history, whiteboard scratchpad — all one click away.

Cozy minigames for breaks

When you need to step away from work without leaving the app: play chess against a built-in AI, beat your office in foosball or flappy bird, jam on a guitar rhythm game, watch fish swim and feed the aquarium, or just doodle on the whiteboard.

Compact mode + monitor dock

Switch to the always-on-top mini window when you need the screen. Or attach the full window to the left or right edge of your monitor as a permanent productivity sidebar — your office, your timer, your stats, always glanceable.

Themes you unlock by working

Earn cash through Pomodoros and unlock 10 themes — solid palettes (Midnight Office, Forest Den, Cherry Blossom), gradient skies (Sunset Lobby, Ocean Tide, Aurora Borealis), and texture finishes (Paper Notebook, Wood Workshop, Marble Lounge). The whole UI re-skins instantly — buttons, backdrops, the office sky behind your sprites, even the mini window.

Track your milestones

25 achievements, from "First Day at Work" to "Pomodoro Empire" — natural progression rewards for first profit, first decor, focus streaks, click champions, and the long climb to level 12. Native Steam achievements with unlocked icons, all syncing to your profile.


Made for the workday

  • Launch on startup, always-on-top, mute when unfocused — settings to fit your real workflow

  • Backup & restore your save as a .mybiz file — never lose progress

  • Hourly grandfather clock chimes (optional)

  • Light footprint, low CPU — runs alongside your real work tools, not in front of them

Stop pretending you're not going to Pomodoro again tomorrow. MyBiz turns the time you'd spend anyway into something cozy.

In a world where faith has become bureaucracy, marketing, and social control,
Jesualdo and Magdala fight against corporate saints, televised inquisitors,
and monsters born from collective guilt.

Inscryption, and Darkest Dungeon, built around strong religious satire
and tactical turn-based combat.

  • Unique enemies built around readable gameplay gimmicks

  • Narrative choices and roguelike progression

Indulgences are sold through sponsorships,

and the way the world reacts to you.

Mature Content Description
General Themes: DogmaShutdown is a satirical deckbuilder focused on religious criticism, black humor, and institutional satire.

Violence: Combat is turn-based and abstract. While there is no realistic gore or blood, the game features depictions of "public suffering" and mechanical self-damage used as a resource for tactical advantages (e.g., "Passion" and "Sponsor-Friendly Suffering").

Visual Iconography: Imagery includes skulls, religious symbols, and apocalyptical themes like fire and destruction.

Sensitive Topics: The narrative utilizes themes of guilt, sin, and sacrifice. Potential players should be aware of the "Self-damage" mechanic, which is presented through a satirical, stylized lens.

Exclusions: The game does not contain depictions of sexual assault, non-consensual sex, or substance abuse.

store_data.about_the_game:
Pic Talk Nonsense is a casual puzzle game built around the unique charm of Chinese homophonic wordplay.

In each level, you are presented with an image that looks absurd, surreal, or simply ridiculous at first glance. But every object, gesture, and visual combination in the scene may be part of the answer. By observing the details, breaking down the visual clues, and connecting them through Chinese homophones, puns, idioms, sayings, and internet slang, you must figure out the hidden phrase.

For example:

  • A wristwatch with a completely white face may hint at “confession”, because the Chinese words for “watch” and “confess” sound alike.

  • A paper deer wearing a saddle may point to “calling a deer a horse”, a classic Chinese idiom.

  • Worn-out clothes and torn pockets may hide an answer built from word associations tied to “clothes” and “pocket.”

There are no complicated controls and no stressful time limits. You can take your time to observe, think, and test your ideas. The experience feels like flipping through an interactive book of bizarre visual riddles, constantly moving between “How could that possibly be the answer?” and “Wait… that actually makes perfect sense.”

Features

Guess Chinese Homophone Puzzles

Every level is built around a Chinese wordplay-based answer. The solution might be a short phrase, a four-character idiom, an everyday saying, or even an internet meme.

Solve Visual Brain Teasers

The image is not just decoration. It is the puzzle itself. Object placement, character actions, and strange combinations all serve as clues.

Relaxed, No-Pressure Gameplay

No timers. No punishment for wrong attempts. Just observe at your own pace and enjoy the process of figuring things out.

Fun to Play Alone or Together

Some answers click instantly, while others take a surprising leap of logic. It is perfect for solo play, but also great for guessing together with friends or family.

A Puzzle Experience Rooted in Chinese Language Humor

The game is deeply inspired by Chinese linguistic culture, featuring homophones, double meanings, idioms, sayings, character associations, and online slang.

You May Enjoy This Game If You:

  • like puns, dad jokes, and brain teasers

  • enjoy picture-based word guessing games or light puzzle games

  • want a funny, relaxing, low-pressure experience

  • love discussing ridiculous answers with friends

  • want to try a puzzle game built around Chinese language and humor

A crimson star fell upon Luoyang, and the world knew no more dawn. In this eternal night, you are a warlord — and your stronghold is the last light in the darkness.

⚔ Hex Grid Strategy

Command the battlefield on a hexagonal honeycomb map. Terrain, positioning, and adjacency bonuses create strategic depth far beyond traditional grid-based tower defense. Procedurally generated maps ensure every run demands fresh tactical thinking.

🃏 Deckbuilding with Synergy

True power comes not from stacking numbers, but from mechanisms that create qualitative transformation:

  • Projectile Build — Portal loops, double tiles, absorber bursts — screen-filling bullet hell

  • Melee Build — Chain attacks, sword qi projection, qi bursts — infinite blade works

  • Spell Build — Frost + Fire + Lightning + Poison — elemental resonance storms

  • Control Build — Slow, Freeze, Petrify, Time Stop — enemies never reach the stronghold

  • Economy Build — Invest early, explode late — resource supremacy

🏯 24 Attack Buildings · Card Merge Upgrades

  • Projectile: Arrow Tower, Crossbow, Catapult, Musket Tower, Shotgun Tower...

  • Spell: Fire Tower, Frost Tower, Lightning Tower, Poison Tower, Chain Lightning...

  • Melee: Blade Barracks, Spear Barracks, Whirlwind Barracks, Axe Barracks...

  • Trap: Spike Trap, Fire Pit, Minefield, Net Trap...

  • Summon: Skeleton Tower...

Merge two identical cards to upgrade: Common → Rare → Fine → Epic. Each tier unlocks new abilities that transform your buildings!

🦸 12 Three Kingdoms Heroes

  • Zhao Yun — Projectile enhancer, "Seven In, Seven Out" doubles attack speed

  • Guan Yu — Melee powerhouse, "Slay Hua Xiong" area burst

  • Zhang Fei — AoE burst, "Block the Bridge" creates terrain

  • Zhuge Liang — Special card master, "Eight Formations" global trigger

  • Lü Bu — Extreme attacker, 8 building slots + "Unmatched" burst

  • Diao Chan — Debuff controller, "Moonlight Dance" charm & stun

  • Mi Zhu — Economy developer, shop discounts + output boosts

  • Hua Tuo — Sustain healer, buy with health + resurrection

  • Zhou Yu — Spell burst, "Chibi Flames" fire wall

  • Cao Cao — Balanced all-rounder, "Hold the Emperor" gold burst

  • Sun Shangxiang — Rapid fire, "Arrow Barrage" triple shots

  • Huang Zhong — Precision sniper, "Dingjun Slash" true damage

Each hero has a unique passive skill, active skill, and 5 exclusive cards that redefine your build!

👹 60+ Enemy Types · 30 Waves

From Yellow Turban mobs to Xiliang Iron Cavalry, from Nanman War Elephants to Ghost Armies — 30 waves of escalating threats. 5 legendary bosses guard key waves:

  • Wave 10 — Zhang Jiao, the Grand Teacher

  • Wave 15 — Zhang Bao & Zhang Liang

  • Wave 20 — Lü Bu, the God of War

  • Wave 25 — Dong Zhuo, the Tyrant

  • Wave 30 — Dong Zhuo Awakened, the Demon King

12 enemy traits + 10 affixes create infinite combinations!

📈 5 Difficulty Levels · Endless Mode

  • Casual (10 waves) — Beginner friendly

  • Normal (15 waves) — Learn the mechanics

  • Hard (20 waves) — Standard experience

  • Nightmare (25 waves) — Enemies gain random traits

  • Hell (30 waves) — Ultimate challenge

Unlock Endless Mode after clearing any difficulty — exponentially scaling enemies test your limits!

✨ More Features

  • 60+ functional cards: Resource, Amplify, Debuff, Special, Enhancement

  • 6 terrain types: Plains, Hills, Mountains, Rivers, Forests, Lakes

  • Wilderness system: Risk-reward decisions

  • Shop system: Buy, refresh, upgrade — strategic economy

  • 85+ achievements: Clear, Kill, Build, Collect, Challenge, Hidden

  • 23 languages supported

⚙ Core Mechanics

  • Key Rule: Enemies only move toward your stronghold — they never attack buildings. Place defenses boldly!

  • Two-Phase Loop: Deploy phase (no time limit) → Battle phase (auto-attack + hero skills)

  • Session Length: 45-90 minutes per run

store_data.about_the_game:
Step into a fantasy world rooted in the myths and spirits of Yoruba, Candomblé, and the wider Afro-Brazilian tradition. Crowned Sun is a 3D isometric MMORPG that draws on the warmth and craft of classic online RPGs like Ragnarok Online, Tree of Savior, and Final Fantasy XIV — and gives them a setting almost no other game has dared to.

You arrive in the Mirage Kingdom as one of four peoples — Human, Iwin, Egbere, or Ere — each with their own myth, identity, and feel in combat. Build your hero across two parallel tracks: a Base Level that grows as you adventure, and a Job Level that defines the path you walk. Train your skills in the plazas of Ifadun, hunt through forests and ruins under a sun crowned in legend, and find your place in a community built around the orixás.

Crowned Sun is a love letter to the MMOs that shaped a generation — and a celebration of stories that fantasy rarely gets to tell.

Key Features

  • Afro-Brazilian fantasy world. Locations, races, and lore inspired by Yoruba mythology, the orixás, and Brazilian folklore — built with care, not exoticism.
  • Four playable peoples. Choose between Human (versatile, resilient), Iwin (forest-touched spirits), Egbere (shadow-bound damage dealers who trade defense for raw power), and Ere (childlike spirits with their own twist).
  • Classic dual-leveling. Earn Base Levels through adventure and Job Levels through your chosen class — the deep, layered progression that made Ragnarok Online and Tree of Savior unforgettable.
  • A living world of MMO systems. Parties, guilds, friends lists, pets, mercenaries, mounts, instanced Spirit Trials, large-scale Spirit War battles, mail, achievements, daily login rewards, and a Party Finder to bring it all together.
  • Orisha Echoes. A homage to the orixás and their forces, woven into the systems and progression of the world.
  • 3D isometric art with handcrafted heart. Cel-shaded characters, lush biomes, stone shrines wrapped in greenery, and a soundtrack drawn from the rhythms of the diaspora.
  • Cross-platform. Windows, macOS, and Linux/SteamOS support — bring the kingdom with you.

The Mirage Kingdom

A land of carved stone, sun temples, and woven prophecy. Towns hum with conversation; the wilderness hums with something older. Every quest is a thread, every region a story, and every orixá a memory you can find your way back to.

Who It's For

If you grew up on Ragnarok Online or Tree of Savior, if you spent late nights in classic Final Fantasy XIV cities, if you've ever wished a fantasy MMO would look beyond the same European myths — Crowned Sun is being made for you.

store_data.about_the_game:
The "content moderator." is a management simulation horror game where you sort through social media posts and delete the forbidden ones.

Story

Your mother has only 7 days left to live.

Her surgery costs 1 million yen. To earn the money, you take on a shady job.

Tasks

Review an endless stream of images. "Allow" the clean ones and "Delete" the cursed ones.

Healthcare

This job takes a massive toll on your mental health. Take breaks, play games, or take medication to maintain your sanity. Once you save up enough money, investing in stress-relief items or new games is highly recommended.

Boss

Never let your boss catch you slacking off. If you're caught, your rating will drop, and eventually, you'll be fired. Always watch your back when taking a break.

Pay

Do the work, collect your pay, and hit 1 million yen within 7 days. You can save it all or spend it on items—it's your call. Just don't forget why you're really here.

Features

  • Gameplay built around the concept of a content moderator

  • An eerie blend of retro UI and realistic imagery

  • Most of the basic controls are handled with the mouse.

  • Multiple endings

store_data.about_the_game:
Tisis heavily focuses on storytelling and has a deep philosophical background inspired by the Ancient Greeks worldview of Hubris that leads to Tisis, the philosophical works of Nietzsche and Schopenhauer and the fictional works of Lovecraft, Bierce, Ligotti and many more.

The story revolves around World War 2 soldier-professor joining the Allied operation in Antarctica, called Operation Tabarin, to counter the Nazis operation of Ahnenerbe to find a mystical artifact that will be used to win the War. There they uncover The King in Yellow, a play that, when read, drives one to insanity. After 6 years, the game starts with the character in a Lunatic Asylum, with its patients being all the soldiers and sailors that went mad in the Antarctica Expedition. There he must prevent the King in Yellow, the main antagonist of the play, from achieving his goals to instill madness and terror to the world.

Gameplay

Tisis is a first-person psychological horror game focused on exploration, environmental storytelling, and a deeply narrative-driven experience. Players uncover disturbing clues and fragmented memories as they descend into a world shaped by madness and cosmic terror, revealing the influence of The King in Yellow. Sanity is a core mechanic: remaining in complete darkness gradually drains the protagonist’s mind, forcing players to carefully navigate between shadow and light as reality slowly unravels around them.

store_data.about_the_game:
Deadlight Maze

Deadlight Maze is a tense horror maze experience where survival depends on strategy, awareness, and quick reactions. Explore dangerous mazes filled with deadly traps, dark corridors, and relentless zombies searching for their next target.

Use your flashlight’s color system to freeze zombies before they reach you. Match the correct light color to stop enemies temporarily, create safe paths, and survive long enough to escape the maze. Every wrong move can attract nearby zombies, forcing players to think carefully about movement and timing.

As you progress, each maze introduces new dangers, tighter spaces, faster enemies, and more challenging trap layouts. Portable lights can also be used to create temporary safe zones and block zombie movement through certain areas.

How to Play?

In Deadlight Maze, zombies are frozen based on matching colors—when your flashlight color matches a zombie’s color, it freezes them. You move through a maze while avoiding zombies and traps, using your controls to walk, run, and explore. Your flashlight is your main tool, so aim it carefully to stop enemies at the right moment. Zombies can see you at a close range and can hear your movement and footsteps (based on surface) at a medium range, so moving smart and staying quiet is important.

You can also pick up portable lights, carry them, and place them anywhere. By setting the correct color on these lights, you can block paths so zombies can’t pass through or follow you. Your goal is to survive and reach the end of the level or complete simple objectives. Use your flashlight and placed lights wisely to control zombies and stay alive.

Features

  • Horror maze gameplay focused on survival and tension

  • Color-based flashlight mechanic to freeze zombies

  • Multiple maze layouts with increasing difficulty

  • Deadly traps that require timing and precision

  • Portable lights and strategic survival mechanics

  • Atmospheric dark environments

  • Single-player experience

Can you survive the darkness and escape the maze?

store_data.about_the_game:
You work in a remote underwater facility somewhere deep beneath the ocean.

Most days feel the same. Check equipment, repair broken systems, respond to maintenance requests, and keep the station running. Quiet work, far away from the surface.

But lately, things have started to feel off.

Strange sounds travel through the station. Equipment breaks without explanation. Conversations start to feel uneasy. And sometimes, the darkness outside feels harder to ignore than it should.

In The Deepest Shift, you carry out routine work inside and outside an underwater facility while something slowly changes around you. Travel through the deep, inspect damaged systems, and try to make sense of things that don’t quite add up.

Sometimes, it’s easier not to ask too many questions.



Features

  • Psychological horror focused on atmosphere and tension

  • Perform routine maintenance tasks in an underwater facility

  • Explore an isolated station deep beneath the ocean

  • Retro  visuals

  • Slow-building horror and unsettling moments

store_data.about_the_game:
Observation Protocol is a first person psychological horror game about doing your job somewhere you shouldn't be.

You are stationed at an external monitoring post, watching camera feeds of a liminal office space - a facility that exists outside of normal space, scheduled for permanent closure by the organization that found it. Your task is simple: observe, identify, and document anomalies before the final containment procedure begins.

Then the power cuts.

With your monitoring equipment down, protocol demands you enter physically and continue your work from the inside. Armed with only a camera, you must move through the empty offices and corridors, photograph what doesn't belong, and get out before the organization completes closure - not locking a door, but severing the connection to this place entirely.

Document enough anomalies and the space stabilizes. Stay too long and it won't matter.

Get out in time.

A liminal horror experience. PSX aesthetic. First person. Singleplayer.

store_data.about_the_game:
Chrome Survivor is our take on an infinitely playable Bullet Heaven. Level up, find items that create interesting synergies, charge beacons to gain more stats, find the shops to purchase items, combine weapons together to create powerful evolutions, and most importantly, annihilate the hordes!

Chrome Survivor currently has 10 playable characters each with their own unique starting weapon and passives.

Overall there are 12 base weapons and 12 weapon evolutions. (Our weapons evolve by combining two level 8 weapons). Not all of them can be combined with each other however.

There are over 90 achievements in game many of which unlock new characters, new items, and maximum cool points.

There are also over 90 items in game to maximize your builds and create awesome synergies, no two runs will feel the same.

There are numerous ways to scale difficulty such as through Psychosis, a stat that directly increases max spawns and enemy scaling, randomized map modifiers players can add to their runs to increase difficulty and rewards, and completing maps unlocks higher tiers of difficulty. We currently have one map "ELECTRIC FOREST", while the others are procedural generated for now. These will be replaced later.

We also have a built in weather system that randomizes between every run, and each type of weather has buffs/debuffs to certain aspects of the game. For instance ASHFALL weather starts the game with +50% Psychosis.

Well, whats the point of all this extra loot? In Chrome Survivor we have implemented an essentially infinite crafting system. Operators gain ranks based on run success and unlock "Augment" slots. These slots can be filled with the pre-made augments you find through play

Or ones you craft yourself.

Hopefully the current features are enough to grab your attention! We look forward to players enjoying the game and joining us through our Early Access journey! Thanks!

store_data.about_the_game:
WHAT is a Sack?

Is it flour? Corn? Potatoes? A philophisical question that has yet to be answered since 1793, but Sack Investigation might just be the closest you will get to being able to grasp such complex subject matter. To understand the sack, you must first become the sack. In it's natural environment, a whimsical wizard tower, you and up to 7 fellow sacks will be thrown forth to investigate and solve puzzles to locate and destroy cursed objects.

Gameplay

Each level will be filled with rooms that change and shift, with enough traps and enemies to keep you on your tassels...eventually. Scrounge around to find Sackels, an unsanctioned unground currency, to purchase upgrades between levels to take your sackness to new heights. Help your friends to solve changing puzzles with limited possibilities! or don't, sacks aren't that significant and neither is what you do. You Are Replaceable. 

Who Is This For?

Do you love buying games for over $70? Do you love constantly buying battle passes? Do you love coming home from work and to wind down for the day, you play the most stress inducing game imaginable? Then this game is not for you. Like you can still legally buy it, I guess, for now. Sack Investigation is for the casuals and people who just really want to be a sack. Its best if you really get into character and brace your self for the emotional depth of the protagonist.

Finally

This is a project born from passion and developed by a small team. Our shared love of sacks really brought us together and we have full intention to bring this game to a worthy standard. Now get ready to go do whatever a sack does!

store_data.about_the_game:
Something on the Floor

A sudden blackout struck an ordinary hotel.

When the power came back on, everyone was gone.

As the caretaker, you enter the hotel to search for the missing people.

But the floors of this place repeat endlessly,

and somewhere inside, something is definitely there.

Survive the Repeating Hotel

『Something on the Floor』 is a story-driven anomaly horror game where you explore endlessly repeating hotel floors, find anomalies, and choose the correct escape route to move on to the next floor.

Each floor hides changes that were not there before.

Find what has changed, understand the rules of the hotel, and continue deeper into its repeating floors.

If you handle an anomaly incorrectly,

or choose the wrong path—

the hotel will begin to remember your mistakes.

Anomalies

In the repeating floors, anything that has changed from its usual state is an anomaly.

Anomalies may appear as tiny, subtle differences, or in forms that are impossible to ignore.

Observe your surroundings carefully.

Find what is wrong, deal with it in the correct way, and move on to the next floor.

Escape Routes

Each floor contains three escape routes.

You must choose the route that fits the situation in order to reach the next floor safely.

Elevator, stairs, emergency exit.

Even on the same floor, the safe path changes every time.

If you made the wrong choice, do not hesitate.

Run.

The Hotel’s Secret

As you repeat the game, collect torn pieces of notes.

These notes record what happened in this hotel, and why you were left behind here.

『Something on the Floor』 features three main endings, as well as a true ending that can only be reached after collecting every clue.

Key Features

  • Observation-based horror gameplay where you find anomalies in repeating hotel floors

  • Three escape routes that must be chosen depending on the situation

  • A threatening presence that reacts to wrong choices and certain conditions

  • Story collection through torn note fragments

  • Three main endings and one true ending

  • A story mode lasting approximately 1–2 hours

Bonus Modes

Even after you complete Story Mode, the hotel does not end.

Various bonus modes are prepared, twisting the rules of the main game in different ways.

Experience Infinity Mode, where you test your survival in endlessly repeating floors,

Speedrun Mode, made for players who have fully mastered the hotel’s rules,

and special modes that let you enjoy the hotel in completely different ways.

Sometimes, instead of running away, you may need to stand your ground.

Sometimes, the developer may appear inside the hotel.

And in one particular mode,

the hotel is ruled by cats.

Do not ask why.

Wishlist

Wishlisting the game is a huge help to the developer.

Depending on wishlist milestones, we plan to expand the game through free updates, including secret rooms, hidden endings, special modes, and more.

Understand the rules of the repeating hotel, follow the traces of the missing people,

and uncover the true reason you were left behind.

store_data.about_the_game:
By day you raid the dungeons. By night they raid your town.

A peaceful farming village. An ancient seal, shattered by earthquakes. Something deep beneath the mountain is waking up — and the only thing standing between it and your town is you, a farmer with a shovel and maybe a little courage.

Sentry is a hybrid action RPG and tower defense set in a hand-crafted pixel-art world. Loot ruined dungeons by day. Forge gear, plant traps, and brace the gates by night. Every dungeon you clear weakens the horde that comes for your town.... but every day you waste, the monsters get closer.

Two games. One loop. No safe nights.

  • Crawl deep, loot fast. Six themed dungeons — the Mines, the Goblin Cave, the Crypt, the Forest Den, the Frozen Depths, and the Shadow Realm — each with five floors of procedurally generated rooms, secret areas, traps, puzzles, and elite-modified monsters guarding chests, crystals, and dark essence.

  • Die in the dungeon, lose the run. No entry fee, no safety net. Push deeper for legendary loot, or recall before the night catches you with nothing.

  • Hold the line at home. Build a kill-box out of 20+ traps and turrets — spike plates, fire ballistas, tesla coils, void rifts — and fight alongside them as monsters pour out of every dungeon path you've opened.

  • Six bosses, three phases each. Corrupted seal guardians with telegraphed mechanics, destructible armor, weak-spot windows, and ultimates that reshape the arena. Beat one and that dungeon is silenced forever.

Three classes. Ten specializations. 77 skills.

Pick your weapon when the mayor hands you one — and then earn the right to specialize.

  • Knight — Berserker rage, Warden shields, or Vanguard charges. Hold the choke.

  • Ranger — Sharpshooter crits, Trapper area denial, or Wind Runner hit-and-run. Own the perimeter.

  • Mage — Archmage meteors, Chronomancer time-warps, Ward Mage barriers, Summoner followers. Erase whole waves.

At level 7, your class branches. Each branch ends in a unique capstone ability you build your whole run around.

The clock is the real boss.

Earthquakes happen on a schedule. You can't stop them. Every five days another dungeon cracks open, another wave of monsters joins the nightly assault, and the town's integrity ticks down whether you were ready or not. Turtle and you'll be buried. Rush and you'll die broke in a dungeon two floors too deep.

Features

  • 6 hand-themed dungeons, 30 floors, 6 unique 3-phase boss fights

  • 42 distinct enemy types across 7 tactical roles, plus an elite modifier system (Molten, Vortex, Reflective, Avenger, Teleporter)

  • Hundreds of variants of armor and weapons

  • Multiple narrative based side quests and dozens of procedural quests

  • 20+ placeable traps and turrets with synergies, blueprints, and targeting modes

  • 3 playable classes, 10 specialization branches, 77 skills

  • A full town economy: blacksmith forging, guild quests, daily bounties, potion upgrades, shop progression

  • Procedurally generated dungeons built on hand-authored room templates — every run is new, but every room is intentional

  • Pixel art, screen shake, damage numbers, and the satisfying chunk of a sword hitting something that shouldn't be there

  • Full controller support (PS / Xbox), keyboard + mouse

The farmer didn't ask to be a legend.

But the seal is broken. The town is counting on you. And something down there knows your name.

Will Millbrook still be standing when the last earthquake hits?
